arxiv.org/abs/2606.30721.title: SHARP -- A spectrograph proposal to fully exploit ELT capabilities and look beyond JWST
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30721.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30721v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs), with their large apertures and cutting-edge Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (MCAO) systems, promise to deliver data that is both sharper and deeper than even the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) across large fields. SHARP is a concept study for a near-IR (0.95-2.45 $\mu$m) spectrograph specifically designed to fully exploit the collecting area and angular resolution capabilities of the upcoming ESO's ELT. The instrument concept is driven by the goal of tackling the most important questions in astrophysics and cosmology, from exploring primordial galaxies to studying the formation of young stellar object and planetary systems in the nearby dust-enshrouded regions, bridging the gap between the local and the distant Universe. This requires versatility to accommodate diverse observational needs. SHARP is composed of two main units: NEXUS, a Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS) optimized for detecting the faintest sources, and VESPER, a multi-object Integral Field Unit (multi-IFU) designed for brighter ones. This article provides an overview of the scientific design drivers, the solutions developed to meet them, and the resulting optical design that achieves the required performance.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.30727.title: A new era for Dual AGN science with SHARP
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30727.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30727v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The search for and the characterization of ultra-compact dual active galactic nuclei (AGN) are among the hottest topics of current extragalactic astrophysics. These systems involve two accreting massive black holes (MBHs) embedded within the same host galaxy, with relative projected separations from a few hundred pc down to a few pc. They are central to understanding hierarchical galaxy formation, black hole growth and demographics, and accretion-feedback coupling in the most extreme interaction phases. Even more compellingly, such tight pairs are the most direct precursors of gravitationally bound binary MBHs (sub-pc scale separation), which are among the loudest emitters of gravitational waves (GWs) in the low-frequency ranges. SHARP will deliver the first statistical census and physical characterization of ultra-compact dual AGN up to cosmic distances, finally bridging the observational gap between kpc-scale pairs and sub-pc GW-emitting binaries, and enabling a breakthrough understanding of MBH growth, feedback and co-evolution across cosmic time.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.30763.title: A SHARP Look at Quenching and Bulge-Disk Growth in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30763.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30763v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The physical mechanisms that quench star formation in massive galaxies remain poorly understood. At cosmic noon (1<3), when star formation and AGN activity peak, galaxies rapidly evolve from star-forming disks into quiescent, bulge-dominated systems. While quenching correlates with stellar mass and bulge growth, the causal link between bulge assembly, star-formation suppression, and feedback processes remains unclear. Stellar population analysis from spatially resolved spectroscopy of galaxies caught during quenching is crucial to advance on this issue. We show that the SHARP-VESPER Integral-Field Spectrograph (IFS) can efficiently fill this gap by combining ELT-class sensitivity, 31 mas spatial resolution (>3x sharper than JWST) and broad near-IR wavelength coverage with 12-IFU multiplexing. This will enable, for the first time, a simultaneous bulge-disk decomposition of stellar populations and spatially resolved mapping of ionised gas in massive galaxies (log $M_*/M_{\odot}\geq 11$) at 2.2<3.5, targeting systems on the main sequence shortly before quenching or already in the green valley. With typical exposure times of 15 hr, we will obtain S/N>15-20 per spectral resolution element, on the inner bulge, and outer disk extracted spectral continuum, and S/N>5 for nebular lines ([OII], H$\beta$, [OIII], H$\alpha$) on sub-kpc scales. These observations will allow us to reconstruct independent bulge and disk star-formation histories, ages, metallicities, and $\alpha$-enhancements, while mapping spatially resolved star formation, gas kinematics, and feedback-driven outflows. By directly comparing the timing of bulge growth and star-formation suppression across galaxy components, this programme will test whether quenching proceeds inside-out, distinguish fast and slow quenching pathways, and link structural transformation to feedback processes in the most massive galaxies at cosmic noon.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.31189.title: Probing IMF Variations in High-Redshift Early-Type Galaxies with SHARP
arxiv.org/abs/2606.31189.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.31189v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The stellar initial mass function (IMF), which describes the distribution of stellar masses at birth, is a fundamental ingredient in shaping galaxy evolution. Recent observations indicate that the IMF varies between galaxies, depending on their mass, morphology, and stellar content. In local early-type galaxies (ETGs), spectroscopy, dynamics, and lensing reveal bottom-heavy IMFs in dense central regions, with radial gradients toward a Milky Way-like distribution in the outskirts. Yet, the chemical enrichment of massive ETGs implies a dominant role of massive stars during their early formation phases. These findings can be reconciled if the IMF evolves over cosmic time -- initially more top-heavy to enable rapid enrichment, and later dominated by long-lived, low-mass stars. Directly measuring the IMF at z>1 is therefore essential to test such time-dependent IMF scenarios, including variations in the dwarf-to-giant and stellar mass-to-light ratios. To date, no direct observational confirmation of these IMF variations -- or of their physical origin -- has been obtained. The SHARP spectrograph on the E-ELT, with unprecedented spatial resolution and sensitivity compared to facilities such as JWST, and broader spectral coverage than other E-ELT instruments, will enable spatially resolved spectroscopy of IMF-sensitive features in high-redshift ETGs up to z~3, providing unique insights into the origin of the non-universal IMF in massive galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.06604.title: Fast Graph-based Higher-Order Clustering Statistics on the GPU
arxiv.org/abs/2607.06604.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.06604v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a significant update to GRAMSCI (GRAph Made Statistics for Cosmological Information; Sabiu et al. 2019), an algorithm for the fast computation of the general $N$-point spatial correlation function of any discrete point set. Version 2 adds several features. We replace the binary-search inner loop ($O(m\log m)$ per hub-spoke pair, $m$ being the mean neighbor count) with a merge-walk algorithm that reduces the inner loop to $O(m)$. We implement a parity-decomposed 4pCF that separates the signal into even and odd channels. We estimate the disconnected 4pCF internally on the same graph to return the connected 4pCF. We add a Python/NumPy interface to the Fortran engine. Principally, we present a GPU port of the full query engine (OpenACC): the 3pCF, 4pCF, and parity-decomposed 4pCF kernels run on a single consumer GPU with measured speedups of $2.6\times$ (3pCF) to $9\times$ (4pCF) over a 64-thread CPU node, and out-of-core tiling handles graphs exceeding device memory. We measure a $9\times10^9$-edge BAO-scale 3pCF on a 24 GB card with $\sim 20\%$ overhead. We validate the code against its CPU reference, against analytic injection tests, and on exactly solvable random fields (a non-Gaussian multiplicative cascade and a Gaussian field, whose full and connected 4pCF the estimators reproduce without bias), and demonstrate BAO-scale applications on the DESI DR1 LRG sample (the 3pCF and the full and connected 4pCF over the complete configuration space, both to 150 $h^{-1}$ Mpc).

arxiv.org/abs/2608.01634.title: Inferring Properties of Rotating Core-Collapse Supernovae with Gravitational-Wave Detector Networks
arxiv.org/abs/2608.01634.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.01634v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Core-collapse supernovae are among the most promising yet still undetected sources of gravitational waves. A future detection would provide a direct view of the physical processes occurring deep inside a collapsing star. In this work, we investigate how networks of current and future gravitational-wave detectors can constrain the properties of rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae using their characteristic core-bounce and early post-bounce signals. Using deep-learning techniques, we estimate the peak frequency, rotation rate, and signal amplitude from noisy detector data and compare the performance of different detector-network configurations. We find that detector networks improve both parameter recovery and sky coverage. For current-generation networks, estimation of the peak frequency is possible out to about 15 kpc, while the rotation rate remains recoverable out to distances exceeding 100 kpc. Third-generation observatories extend these distances by approximately a factor of three to four.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.06328.title: A unified modeling of X-ray and gamma-ray spectro-polarimetric data: the case of Cygnus X-1
arxiv.org/abs/2608.06328.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.06328v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent X-ray and soft gamma-ray spectro-polarimetric observations of black hole X-ray binaries, such as Cygnus X-1, reveal discrepancies that challenge current models of accretion and high-energy emission. We present a general framework for broadband spectro-polarimetric modeling that simultaneously fits spectral and polarization data from independent instruments across different energy bands. The method robustly combines measurements with different energy binning and statistical significance while accounting for energy-dependent polarization mixing between model components. Applied to Cygnus X-1 over the 2 keV-2 MeV range, it provides an improved characterization of the soft gamma-ray hard-tail and constrains the optically thin synchrotron cutoff energy to $(2.8^{+0.6}_{-0.8}) \times 10^{2}$ keV. We discuss the implications for non-thermal electron acceleration in the context of Bohm diffusion and synchrotron cooling, and propose a new explanation for the observed polarization misalignment based on magnetic field helicity and Doppler boosting. The framework is broadly applicable to multi-instrument spectro-polarimetric analyses.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.29698.title: Gemini and Apache Point Multi-band Optical Imaging Characterization of Fragmenting Long-period Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
arxiv.org/abs/2608.29698.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.29698v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present results from multi-band g, r, and i, observations of C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) taken with the Gemini North 8.1-m/GMOS imager on 2025 December 6 and December 24, and u, g, r, i, and z observations with the Astrophysical Research Consortium (ARC) 3.5-m/ARCTIC imager on 2025 December 8. We identify at least four distinct fragments in the Gemini and ARC images, designated as A, C, D, and E in these data taken between 2025 December 6 and 24. Color indices are determined from the December 8 ARC observations of fragments A and C, and from the Gemini observations on December 24 for A, C, and D. K1 has an unusually blue g-r color of $\sim$0.40. The color difference between the comet and its fragments at the two epochs may be explained by particle size and light-scattering effects. We used the Gemini observations to calculate dust mass-loss rates for fragments A, C, and D. We conclude that C/2025 K1 has moderate dust mass-loss rates for millimeter-sized dust of $\sim$50 kg/s for the A and C fragments.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.30116.title: Moment-based formulas for the transport coefficients
arxiv.org/abs/2608.30116.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.30116v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The coefficients of the transport equations, describing the propagation features, are particularly important in astrophysics, interplanetary physics, and experimental plasma physics. In this paper, the variable-dependent diffusion coefficients are investigated. For the momentum transport equations, we find that the coefficients are related to statistical quantities, some of which are new. In addition, these coefficients take logarithmic forms, which are different from the results derived in previous papers. For isotropic pitch-angle scattering, we also obtain a formula that takes a logarithmic form. For fractional transport equations, the coefficients expressed in terms of the moments are obtained from the governing equations.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.04318.title: Composition gradients in sub-Neptunes: K2-18 b and TOI-270 d as case studies
arxiv.org/abs/2609.04318.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.04318v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18 b and TOI-270 d. We compare purely adiabatic models with distinct layers against models that include composition gradients and stable non-convective regions. We present solutions that are consistent with the observed masses, radii, and atmospheric boundary conditions. We find that composition gradients significantly increase the range of viable interior structures: For example, the interior degeneracy remains substantial even for fixed mass and radius, and the maximum hydrogen-helium (H-He) mass fraction can increase significantly: for K2-18 b by a factor of about three at a 1 bar temperature of 300 K and of about ten at 600 K, and generally by more than an order of magnitude for TOI-270 d. Composition gradients further weaken parameter correlations: for K2-18 b and TOI-270 d, the Spearman rank correlation between the H-He and iron abundances drops from $\sim0.7$ to $\sim0.3$, with a similar weakening between the H-He abundance and the rock-to-iron mass ratio. However, other correlations, such as between the H-He abundance and the water-to-rock mass ratio, persist or even strengthen and remain non-negligible. Purely adiabatic models underestimate the range of plausible compositions and overestimate the impact of more precise measurements, atmosphere models, and host-star constraints on a more accurate characterisation. We suggest that interior models of sub-Neptunes should by default include more complex interiors, such as composition gradients and non-convective regions, when using data for interpreting the planetary structure, formation, and evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.10700.title: Probing the dynamics of extreme galaxies I. Dark matter content in ultra-diffuse galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2609.10700.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.10700v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate the internal structure of two galaxies from the LEWIS sample: the ultra-diffuse galaxy UDG-1 and the extended dwarf LSB-6. Both show coherent stellar rotation combined with a non-negligible fraction of random motion, with no signs of ongoing disturbance. This is the first attempt to constrain the dynamics and dark matter physics of rotation-supported UDGs through integral-field stellar kinematics. We model the galaxies as stellar spheroids with typical dwarf-like thickness embedded in spherical dark matter halos, deriving two-dimensional velocity fields that we compare with the observations in a Bayesian framework. Besides cold dark matter, we test fuzzy, self-interacting, and non-minimally coupled dark matter. The data prefer a cuspy halo in UDG-1 and a cuspless one in LSB-6. All the alternative models remain viable, although current data cannot conclusively discriminate among them. For fuzzy dark matter we obtain mutually consistent boson masses, $m_\alpha = 4.7^{+1.8}_{-1.1} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for UDG-1 and $m_\alpha = 6.3^{+0.4}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for LSB-6. For self-interacting dark matter, LSB-6 yields a robust constraint on the velocity-weighted cross section, $\langle \sigma v\rangle/m = 14.3^{+2.0}_{-1.9}$ cm$^2$ km g$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. For non-minimally coupled dark matter we derive upper bounds on the coupling length, implying marginal deviations from $\Lambda$CDM. Regardless of the model, both galaxies exhibit a dark matter content comparable with halos of typical dwarf galaxies with similar stellar masses. Together with stellar population analyses and globular cluster information, these results support a scenario in which UDG-1 and LSB-6 originate from puffed-up dwarfs. This work is the first in a series exploiting kinematic data of extremely low-surface-brightness galaxies to test fundamental physics, from dark matter to modified theories of gravity.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.12339.title: Stellar bar occurrence in TNG50 and TNG100: disentangling environmental effects and assembly history at z = 0
arxiv.org/abs/2609.12339.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.12339v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In this work, we investigate the dependence of bar presence on environment using TNG50 and TNG100 simulations at z=0. We select disc galaxies within $2 R_{200}$, with stellar mass M$_{\star} \geq 10^{10}$ M$_{\odot}$ (TNG100) and M$_{\star} \geq 10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$ (TNG50). With these criteria, our final samples consist of 1719 and 859 satellite galaxies in TNG100 and TNG50, respectively. The environment is characterised by host halo mass: massive (M$_{\rm h} \geq 10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), intermediate ($10^{13} < \rm M_{\rm h} < 10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), and low-mass haloes (M$_{\rm h} \leq 10^{13}$ M$_{\odot}$). We find that our samples recover the morphology-density relation, with thin disc fractions increasing with cluster-centric distance and decreasing halo mass. The bar fraction and the bar radius normalized by the effective radius decrease mildly with cluster-centric distance, while absolute bar radii remain constant. At fixed distance, the bar fraction increases with halo mass, partly because more massive galaxies reside in more massive haloes. In addition, we find that galaxies with earlier assembly times show a higher bar fraction, especially within $0.5 R_{200}$, suggesting a connection between earlier assembly and a higher probability of hosting a bar. Overall, we find a mild environmental dependence, with a stronger connection to stellar mass and assembly history.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.31543.title: A derived evolution of dark energy from cosmic inhomogeneity confronted with baryon acoustic oscillations and type Ia supernovae
arxiv.org/abs/2609.31543.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.31543v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The volume dynamics of space is a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. It yields a redshift-dependent effective Hubble constant and dark-energy density parameter from the Planck parameters alone. We derive the expansion history $H(z)$ of the framework and show that it is flat $\Lambda$CDM with the cosmological constant replaced by a dark-energy density that grows by 31 percent toward the present, with an effective equation of state $w(0) = -1.21$ approaching $-1$ at high redshift and a present-day age of 13.52 Gyr, 0.3 Gyr younger than in the homogeneous limit. We confront it with the DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and the Pantheon+ type Ia supernovae, with the Hubble constant, the sound horizon and the supernova absolute magnitude free, so that only the shape of $H(z)$ is tested. Relative to $\Lambda$CDM the prediction is disfavored by $\Delta\chi^2 = 65$ with one parameter fewer. A free matter density reduces this to $\Delta\chi^2 = 42$, because each probe alone accommodates the model only with incompatible matter densities (0.35 from the oscillations, 0.54 from the supernovae). Their combination bounds the heterogeneity amplitude to $\sigma_8 < 0.14$ at 95 percent confidence, against the Planck input 0.81; the best fit of the heterogeneous model is its homogeneous limit, flat $\Lambda$CDM. At the leading order currently evaluated, the heterogeneous contribution cannot account for the Hubble tension, and it acts opposite to the evolution of dark energy that current distance data favor.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.31842.title: Correlated Signatures of Plasma Lensing in Fast Radio Bursts
arxiv.org/abs/2609.31842.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.31842v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Plasma lensing has been proposed to explain narrow spectra, multiple burst copies, frequency drifts, interference fringes, and polarization changes in fast radio bursts (FRBs). Because many of these features are not unique to lensing, a convincing identification requires several correlated observables to be reproduced by one lens model. We derive such relations for a one-dimensional Gaussian plasma lens near a fold caustic. We distinguish the phase separation of the merging images from their observable group-delay difference and identify three regimes: resolved burst copies, overlapping images with negligible mutual coherence, and coherent spectral interference. We connect the magnification, image delay, spectral-envelope width, fringe spacing, differential dispersion, time-frequency caustic curvature, and the brightness and ordering of the third image. We derive separate finite-source constraints from large fold magnification and from fringe visibility, and relate the wave-optics magnification scale to the plasma column of the lens. High-contrast fringes simultaneously constrain the source size and the mutual coherence of the two image fields, which constrains the intrinsic coherence of the FRB radiation once the observed spectrum and instrumental bandpass are accounted for. We also derive the conditions for differential Faraday rotation in magnetized lenses. Finally, we show that clean lensing by a volume-filling turbulent screen requires fine tuning between rare strong fluctuations and caustic confusion, suggesting that sparse sheets, filaments, interfaces, or shocked clumps are more promising lensing structures.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.37597.title: TOI-6981 b: a transiting sub-Neptune at the water ice line
arxiv.org/abs/2609.37597.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.37597v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present TOI-6981 b, a cold (Teq= 175^{+6}_{-5} K, assuming an Earth-like albedo) sub-Neptune (Rb=2.51+/-0.11 R_oplus) orbiting on a 60.8 day orbit around around its M4-type host star (R*=0.304 +/- 0.012 R_odot, M*=0.296 +/- 0.026 M_odot, Teff = 3215+/-58K), part of the SPECULOOS TEMPOS program. We validate the planetary nature of TOI-6981 b using ground-based follow-up photometry, statistical validation and high-resolution spectroscopy. At such cold temperatures, TOI-6981 b sits roughly at the location of the water ice line (approx 170 K). Given its orbital period and high transmission spectroscopy metric (TSM=56 +/- 10), it is one of the only planets in the sparsely populated cold planet regime amenable for atmospheric studies with JWST. Therefore, TOI-6981 b could. possibly become a crucial benchmark in cold chemistry studies, tests of Hycean world hypotheses, and drawling parallels to the Solar System's ice giants. Additionally, given its current orbit, it may provide insight into planetary formation and migration at or beyond the water ice line.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.40233.title: An ALMA sub-kiloparsec test of the Kennicutt--Schmidt relation in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at $z\sim2.78$
arxiv.org/abs/2609.40233.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.40233v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: [abridged] Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires resolving cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kpc scales. At z~2-3, near the peak of cosmic star formation, such resolution can generally only be achieved through strong gravitational lensing. We present an ALMA study of SMMJ0658, a 20x-magnified main-sequence star-forming galaxy at z=2.7768 +/- 0.0002, lensed by the Bullet Cluster (z=0.296) into three images. We use 0.2" and 0.6" ALMA Band-3 observations to test the Kennicutt-Schmidt (KS) relation at sub-kpc scales at cosmic noon. Using a JWST-based strong-lensing model of the Bullet Cluster, we reconstruct source-plane CO(3-2) and rest-frame 803um dust-continuum maps down to ~200pc scales. We derive spatially resolved molecular gas and star formation rate surface densities, depletion times, and the scale dependence of the CO-to-dust flux ratio over 200pc-3.2kpc apertures. The 0.2" ALMA data reveal massive, dense star-forming clumps, with Sigma_mol ~1.3-2.3 x 10^3 M_sun pc^-2, Sigma_SFR ~0.5-2.3 M_sun yr^-1 kpc^-2, and tau_dep ~0.82-2.56 Gyr. CO-dust spatial decorrelation produces a strong scale dependence in tau_dep. We find a KS-relation breakdown scale of 0.8 +/- 0.1 kpc, consistent with individual regions tracing distinct stages of the star-formation cycle. The ALMA and JWST data also reveal evidence for a lensed galaxy pair at z~2.78, although whether SMMJ0658 is undergoing an early-stage interaction remains uncertain. Our results show that the apparent universality of the KS relation breaks down once individual star-forming regions are spatially resolved, in line with observations from the local universe to z~1. We extend this picture to z~2.78, providing new insight into the resolved properties of the clumpy cold ISM and the star-formation cycle at cosmic noon.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.08671.title: Boosted Odds: Lower-Point Probes of Parity Violation with Momentum Fields
arxiv.org/abs/2610.08671.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.08671v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Parity-violating initial conditions are uniquely compelling signatures of inflationary dynamics beyond the single-field slow-roll paradigm, and their effects on the distribution of late-time observables can be easily separated from that of gravitational nonlinearities and galaxy formation physics. In this work, we propose using the momentum field, $\mathbf{p} = (1+\delta)\mathbf{v}$, and, in particular, the density-density-momentum bispectrum as a novel probe of primordial parity violation. This class of bispectra greatly complements traditional searches using four-point statistics of the density field, furnishing new observables that can be sensitive to parity-violating physics. At the same time, its lower dimensionality substantially reduces the complexity associated with analysing high-dimensional data vectors and their covariance. We show that the sensitivity of the density-density-momentum bispectrum to parity violation effects persists even if we can only observe the projection of the momentum field along the line-of-sight. We perform a Fisher forecast for the parity-violating amplitude of the ultra-squeezed template in the cross bispectrum of kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) anisotropies and galaxy clustering, and we find that our approach give competitive constraints when compared to existing methods. Our method can be easily co-opted to existing pipelines to study parity violation and, as the galaxy-galaxy-kSZ bispectrum is a key cosmological probe, take advantage of the significant existing efforts dedicated to mitigating systematics and covariance modelling.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.17652.title: Experimental evidence for a physical alteration of fine regolith on near-Sun asteroids
arxiv.org/abs/2610.17652.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.17652v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The surfaces of airless bodies evolve through processes such as (micro-)meteoroid impacts and thermal fatigue, which can modify physical properties such as grain size, porosity, and mineral texture. These properties provide clues as to the evolution of airless surfaces, and understanding them is also necessary for interpreting telescopic observations. Near-Sun asteroids (NSAs), which approach the Sun at heliocentric distances of $\lesssim$0.2 au, are notable targets, as their surfaces are likely modified by intense solar radiation. However, experimental studies of how radiative heating modifies the physical properties of carbonaceous asteroid surfaces remain scarce compared with studies of thermally induced changes in mineral composition and spectra. We simulated near-Sun conditions ($0.09<0.19$ au) in the laboratory using the Space and High-Irradiance Near-Sun Simulator and irradiated CM-type carbonaceous chondrite simulants under vacuum. Brightness changes were monitored in situ with a video camera during heating, and morphology was examined with a stage microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM). The irradiated samples show initial darkening followed by brightening, consolidation, and morphological modifications from sub-micrometer to millimeter scales. The brightness modifications are more consistent with changes in the absorption properties than with variations in surface roughness. SEM imaging of the heated samples shows structures similar to those formed by sintering, which are completely absent in unheated samples. These results suggest that sintering is a likely candidate for the mechanism responsible for the observed consolidation and morphological changes. This work provides experimental evidence to help constrain the surface evolution of NSAs in general, and supports the sintering hypothesis as a possible mechanism proposed for (3200) Phaethon in particular.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.17921.title: A breath of fresh air: Oxygen enhancement from silicate sublimation during early protostellar evolution
arxiv.org/abs/2610.17921.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.17921v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recently, an analog to the t = 0 moment of our Solar System's meteoritic record was identified for the first time around the Class I protostar HOPS-315. Crystalline silicates were found to recondense from SiO gas that cools as it advects upward from a hot thermostat region in the inner midplane. This t=0 moment may be associated with the formation of the first planetesimals in this disk. We explore whether HOPS-68, a Class I protostar with similar properties and system geometries, is engaged in such refractory recondensation as well. A detection of cooler gas-phase SiO in absorption above a hot disk midplane would allow us to achieve this goal, thanks to a previous detection of crystalline silicates. HOPS-68 was observed with the JWST MIRI and NIRSpec, showing multiple bands of molecular absorption. We use local thermal equilibrium slab models to measure the temperature, column density, velocity, and radial location of these bands. The molecular absorption bands of gaseous SiO, H2O, CO2, and 13CO trace a warm molecular inversion layer (300-500 K) at mid-altitudes above the hot disk midplane from 0.3-16 AU, which is consistently blue-shifted with respect to the system velocity by 33-53 km/s. Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of HOPS-68 kinematically resolve an SiO-rich jet and wind. We confirm that HOPS-68, like HOPS-315, is undergoing an epoch analogous to the t=0 moment in the Solar System's planet formation timeline. The detected warm molecular layer traces the base of a disk wind, which carries sublimated material from the thermostat region near 2 AU up into the outer disk. As for HOPS-315, the molecular layer in the inner few AU of HOPS-68 is enhanced in bulk oxygen as a result of this sublimation. Since HOPS-68 is less evolved than HOPS-315, this may indicate a prolonged epoch in protostellar evolution in which such oxygen enhancement occurs.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.24078.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
arxiv.org/abs/2610.24078.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.24078v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.25117.title: MACE: Multigroup-Multiangle Integrated Thermal Compton Scattering Kernel
arxiv.org/abs/2610.25117.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.25117v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a comprehensive set of accurate Compton-scattering tables for use in multigroup, multiangle radiation-transport calculations. The tables contain the exact thermal Compton kernel integrated over incident-energy groups, scattered-energy groups, and angular bins. To generate them, we develop a deterministic integration method in which the pointwise kernel is evaluated with a robust numerical treatment that remains accurate across challenging regions of parameter space. The multidimensional integrals are computed using nested quadratures whose panels adapt to the Compton recoil ridge, its thermal broadening, and the nearly elastic forward-scattering boundary layer. We validate the tabulated results against published kernel profiles, angular and energy moments, mean free paths, multigroup redistribution data, and an independent Monte Carlo estimator. The resulting tables provide the radiation-transport community with accurate, reproducible, and readily usable Compton redistribution matrices and angular moments.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.36170.title: Unveiling the nonthermal environments of NGC 3411 and NGC 5903 through new MeerKAT observations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.36170.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.36170v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Galaxy groups are key laboratories for investigating the interplay between active galactic nucleus (AGN) outbursts and the dynamical processes of the intra-group medium. We aim to characterize the morphology, spectral properties, and magnetic field structure of the diffuse nonthermal radio emission in two peculiar galaxy groups, NGC 3411 and NGC 5903, selected from an originally larger sample, in order to constrain its origin and its connection with the dynamics of the intra-group medium. We present new MeerKAT UHF- and L-band observations of the two groups, complemented by archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data already analyzed in previous works. In NGC 3411, we detect extended radio emission surrounding the central AGN over scales of ~70 kpc, and resolve previously undetected arc-shaped substructures on scales of ~20-30 kpc. This extended component exhibits a relatively uniform steep spectrum ($\alpha$ ~ -1.7). We discuss possible scenarios for its origin, including mini-halos, aged AGN plasma, weak shocks, and the possibility of a radio galaxy observed along the line of sight. In NGC 5903, MeerKAT reveals a complex filamentary morphology, including a previously unknown ring-like structure surrounding the central AGN. Spectral-index mapping shows localized flattening ($\alpha$ ~ -0.9) along the north arc, while polarization data reveal ordered magnetic fields and a patchy rotation measure distribution across the source. Together with the disturbed X-ray morphology, these results support a scenario in which fossil AGN plasma has been redistributed and locally reenergized by group-scale dynamical processes such as turbulence, shear, and weak compression. Our results demonstrate that galaxy groups can host a rich variety of nonthermal phenomena, whose properties can only be fully revealed through the combination of sensitive, high-resolution, and multifrequency radio observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.02919.title: Small-Scale Magnetic Fields of Hyades M Dwarfs: Evolution with Age from the Pleiades to Field Stars
arxiv.org/abs/2611.02919.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.02919v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Small-scale magnetic fields are derived for 18 M-dwarf stars in the Hyades open cluster through an analysis of Zeeman broadening in magnetically sensitive lines from the APOGEE spectra, resulting in mean magnetic fields ranging from 0.7 to 4.3 kG. Comparison with results for field stars hosting exoplanets and stars in the Pleiades open cluster from our previous works reveals distinct distributions of mean magnetic fields, reflecting differences in stellar age. Pleiades stars exhibit stronger fields ($2965\pm632$ G) and are predominantly in the saturated regime, while the roughly 500 million years older Hyades sample has weaker fields ($1925\pm1028$ G) with a larger dispersion, spanning both saturated and unsaturated regimes. Field stars show substantially weaker fields ($573\pm272$ G) and consistently occupy the unsaturated regime. Using the three samples, we derive the relationship between small-scale magnetic field strength and Rossby number, identifying saturation limits for the Rossby number ($\mathrm{Ro_{SAT}}=0.145$) and mean magnetic field ($\langle\mathrm{B}\rangle_{\rm SAT}=2452$ G). Within the Hyades sample, we find that, at a given age, cooler stars tend to have stronger magnetic fields. This trend is less apparent in the other samples, due to the broader age distribution of the field stars and magnetic saturation among the Pleiades stars. Comparisons with isochrones indicate positive correlations between mean magnetic field strength and both stellar radius inflation and photospheric spot coverage. We also find positive correlations between magnetic field strength and chromospheric and coronal activity, with stronger fields associated with larger H$\alpha$ equivalent width excess and higher X-ray-to-bolometric luminosity ratios.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.04557.title: Up in smoke: carbon-destruction in the terrestrial planet-forming region of a young Class I disk
arxiv.org/abs/2611.04557.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.04557v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Earth's surface and deep mantle are strongly depleted in carbon compared to the Sun. Sublimation of solid carbonaceous material in the inner midplanes of young disks could cause this depletion. We study such thermal processing in HOPS-68, a Class I protostar with a rich hydrocarbon spectrum. A companion paper has shown that it is recondensing refractory dust from a hot inner disk region, and that oxygen-bearing species are tracing a warm (300-500 K) molecular layer entrained in a disk-wind. In this work, we analyze the carbon species in the JWST spectrum of this source using local thermal equilibrium slab models. We detect warm (~400 K) HCN and C2H2 at the base of a disk wind, as well as colder (~40 K) C4H2, CH3, and CS in the outer disk or outflow cavity wall. Additionally, 13CCH2, CH4, and C6H2 are detected, while ALMA observations reveal C2H tracing the outflow cavity walls. We suggest that in a "refractory carbon destruction zone" in the inner disk, carbon-bearing species are released from the grains, possibly contributing to the observed carbon depletion of Earth. The disk wind then redistributes carbon carried by HCN and C2H2 from the inner disk to the colder outer disk, where UV-induced gas-phase reactions with C2H in the outflow cavity walls could produce the aliphatic carbon chains seen. This result implies that the Warm Carbon Chain Chemistry (WCCC, e.g. N. Sakai & S. Yamamoto 2013) might trace outflows rather than infall. The formation of aliphatic chains in the disk wind could promote the abundant aliphatic organics found in meteorites and asteroids.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.04676.title: Missing Outer Rings in the exoALMA Sample: Physical Mechanisms Suppressing Dust Ring Formation Despite Strong Pressure Bumps
arxiv.org/abs/2611.04676.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.04676v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The exoALMA survey has revealed candidate gas pressure bumps at radii beyond the observed millimetre continuum discs in several protoplanetary systems, raising the question of whether these regions could host undetected dust structures. We investigate this for nine of the exoALMA discs by reconstructing gas surface density profiles from midplane pressure gradient measurements derived from $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO ALMA Band 7 observations. We evolve the dust using DustPy across a grid of turbulence and fragmentation parameters ($\alpha \in \{10^{-4}, 10^{-3}\}$; $v_\mathrm{frag} \in \{1, 10\}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$), followed by radiative transfer calculations with RADMC-3D to give predictions for the continuum emission. We find that the dominant outcome across the explored parameter space is efficient outer dust trapping, leading to prominent outer continuum rings that should be detectable at ALMA Band 7, in tension with the observations. The $^{13}$CO-based reconstructions almost universally produce detectable outer rings, whereas the $^{12}$CO-based reconstructions show more variation. We further test delayed formation of the outer pressure bump and enhanced outer-disc turbulence as possible suppression mechanisms of ring formation. Enhanced turbulence weakens the predicted outer continuum emission most effectively, although the efficiency of the mechanism depends on the system explored and on where the turbulence transition is placed. Delayed bump formation generally does not prevent rapid outer dust accumulation.

arxiv.org/abs/2511.14581.title: Online learning of subgrid-scale models for quasi-geostrophic turbulence in planetary interiors
arxiv.org/abs/2511.14581.excerpt:
arXiv:2511.14581v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Machine learning approaches to subgrid-scale (SGS) modeling are now well established in atmospheric and oceanic applications. Among these, online end-to-end learning, where the differentiable solver participates in the training, has shown particular promise. Yet existing studies are largely restricted to idealised periodic domains, with no mechanical boundaries, precluding them from addressing the dynamics of bounded rotating flows relevant to planetary interiors. Here we consider two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence in a rapidly rotating annular bounded domain. We examine three configurations varying the geometry of the container and the rotation rate. The system exhibits key features such as zonal jets, Rossby waves, and, in the spherical shell geometry, a slow quasi-periodic inward drift of the jets. The spectral properties of the zonal and non-zonal flow can be understood in the framework of zonostrophic turbulence theory. We develop a differentiable solver for this system, which allows us to train SGS models online, over a time span of one turnover time, using coarse-grained data from direct numerical simulations. In all cases, a SGS model trained on a single turnover time accurately reproduces global integrated diagnostics, energy spectra as well as long-term dynamical behaviours, such as jet migration, occurring on timescales which exceed the training window by one order of magnitude. The online-trained model further outperforms classical hyperdiffusivity and Leith closure schemes, for which reducing the radial resolution is impractical. The resulting speed-up paves the way to further investigations of long-term geophysical fluid processes beyond the reach of direct numerical simulations.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.21607.title: Direction-of-arrival estimation of a gravitational wave by correlations between quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data
arxiv.org/abs/2602.21607.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.21607v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Can we estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of a gravitational wave (GW) signal from pulsar timing array observations? The present paper addresses the inverse problem, for which we consider quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data due to GWs from a dominant isolated source such as a binary of supermassive black holes over an isotropic stochastic background. Correlations between the quadrupole moments are discussed as a possible alternative to the matched filtering technique, where the correlations between pulsar pairs over the full sky are taken into account. The correlations turn out to be in the form of a three-dimensional traceless matrix with rank 3 that can be closely related with a projection tensor for the GW. Thereby, we demonstrate that the rank-3 matrix allows to estimate the DOA of the GW without assuming a template bank nor a priori Gaussian noise. A mean over the celestial sphere is adopted instead of the pulsar averaging. A weighted average is used for a non-uniform distribution of pulsars on the sky, for which the Voronoi tessellation is employed to numerically calculate an area-weighted mean. In expectation of the forthcoming Square Kilometre Array, DOA estimation errors are also examined.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.13002.title: Cosmologically viable non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity: explicit models, $\Lambda$CDM limit and observational constraints
arxiv.org/abs/2604.13002.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.13002v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of a phenomenologically relevant subclass of non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG), in which the background dynamics is encoded in a single function of the Hubble parameter. This framework provides a minimal and theoretically consistent extension of general relativity, incorporating higher-curvature effects while preserving second-order field equations and avoiding higher-derivative instabilities. We first establish the general conditions for cosmological viability and construct explicit realizations, including polynomial, quartic, power-law and non-polynomial models, demonstrating how different functional forms lead to distinct expansion histories. Focusing on the quartic and power-law cases, we investigate their late-time cosmological evolution, showing that they exhibit a matter-dominated epoch followed by a dark-energy-dominated epoch, and give rise to an effective dark-energy sector of geometric origin, with dynamical equation-of-state behavior that can lie in the quintessence or phantom regime. We then confront the models with observational data from Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, using a Bayesian MCMC analysis. We find that both models are fully compatible with the considered data and reproduce the late-time expansion history with a quality of fit comparable to that of $\Lambda$CDM, although the current observations do not provide statistically significant evidence for a departure from the concordance scenario. Our results demonstrate that NPQTG offers a simple and efficient framework for describing late-time cosmic acceleration with dynamical dark energy, while maintaining theoretical consistency and observational viability.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.28715.title: Accurate waveforms for generic planar-orbit binary black holes: The multipolar effective-one-body model SEOBNRv6EHM
arxiv.org/abs/2605.28715.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.28715v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient waveform models are required to infer the parameters of compact binaries from their gravitational wave (GW) emission. Among these parameters, orbital eccentricity serves as a smoking gun for dynamical formation channels and must be accounted for to avoid systematic errors in GW analyses. Here, we present SEOBNRv6EHM, a time-domain, multipolar waveform model for binaries on generic planar orbits, calibrated to quasi-circular (QC) numerical-relativity (NR) simulations from the SXS collaboration. In addition to the dominant $(2,2)$ mode, the model provides the $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,2)$, $(4,4)$, and $(4,3)$ multipoles for the full inspiral-merger-ringdown process of coalescing binaries, as well as for dynamical captures and scattering encounters. The model is built within the effective-one-body (EOB) framework, and it employs novel resummations of the radiation-reaction force and waveform modes. We validate its accuracy through comparisons against 592 QC, 319 eccentric, one dynamical-capture, and two scattering SXS NR waveforms, and through scattering-angle comparisons against 61 SXS NR simulations. For QC and small-eccentricity binaries, its accuracy is comparable to previous-generation SEOBNRv5 models. For highly eccentric systems, however, SEOBNRv6EHM attains unprecedented accuracy, with waveform mismatches remaining below or close to $ 2\% $ across the total mass range $ 20-200\, \mathrm{M}_\odot $ for eccentricities up to $\sim 0.9$ at 14 periastron passages before merger. Additionally, SEOBNRv6EHM achieves waveform-generation walltimes that are $ 2 - 8 $ times faster than other state-of-the-art EOB eccentric models, enabling efficient and accurate applications in GW astronomy.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.12549.title: Tachyonic Encore: A universal shift of inflationary observables
arxiv.org/abs/2606.12549.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.12549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We propose a generic mechanism applicable to single-field inflaton models in which a light axion spectator, initialized near the hilltop of its potential, reshapes inflationary observables through purely gravitational multi-field dynamics. During inflation the axion is frozen and the background follows an effectively single-field trajectory. After inflation ends, the axion rolls, inducing a turn in field space and transient tachyonic phases of the isocurvature mode. The resulting ``tachyonic encore'' occurs entirely on super-horizon scales. These phases generate a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppressing the tensor-to-scalar ratio and shifting the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts at horizon crossing. We show that these effects can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints. The same dynamics predict local non-Gaussianity, $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, within reach of upcoming surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.23307.title: Primordial Black Holes from Vector-Induced Curvature Perturbations Sourced by Primordial Magnetic Fields
arxiv.org/abs/2606.23307.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.23307v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generating an appreciable abundance of primordial black holes (PBHs) requires a substantial enhancement of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales. In this Letter, we propose a new post-inflationary mechanism in which such an enhancement arises during a stiff, or kination, epoch. The mechanism is driven by metric vector perturbations sourced by the vector component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor associated with primordial magnetic fields (PMFs). Since these first-order vector modes remain approximately constant during kination, they act as persistent nonlinear sources for second-order scalar perturbations. We show that the resulting vector-induced curvature perturbations are amplified toward the infrared cutoff of the kination band and exhibit the characteristic scaling $\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}(k)\propto k^{-5}$. As a concrete realization, we consider PMFs generated in a Ratra-type magnetogenesis scenario and find that the induced curvature perturbations can produce PBHs with an abundance large enough to constitute a substantial fraction of the dark matter.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.29189.title: Stable Ballistic Prograde Cyclers in the Three-Body Problem
arxiv.org/abs/2606.29189.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.29189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We report the first continuous families of stable, ballistic, prograde cycler orbits in the circular restricted three-body problem: periodic trajectories that alternately undergo temporary capture and orbit each primary. We construct continuous families of symmetric cyclers from intersections of the stable and unstable manifold tubes of the $L_1$ Lyapunov orbit and exhibit stable examples across more than two orders of magnitude in mass ratio, from the Sun-Jupiter regime to the equal-mass limit. Linear stability separates naturally into planar and out-of-plane components. A planar-stable branch of every computed family is created simultaneously with a hyperbolic branch in a saddle-center bifurcation of the return map at the family's maximal Jacobi constant, while out-of-plane instability occurs only through isolated parametric resonances. Every computed family contains a subfamily that is linearly stable to both planar and out-of-plane perturbations. These stable cyclers persist into the full three-body problem for sufficiently small third mass. We conjecture that saddle-center birth is universal among cycler families, suggesting that stable cyclers are a generic feature of three-body dynamics.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.00072.title: Precision Solar System Dynamics for Ultralight Dark Matter Search
arxiv.org/abs/2607.00072.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.00072v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Ultralight dark matter exhibits an order-one density fluctuation at the scale of its wavelength. This density fluctuation exists across the entire dark matter halo and interacts with stars and planets, perturbing their motion via gravitational interactions. We investigate the possibility of using precision solar system dynamics to search for ultralight dark matter. We examine this possibility with interplanetary radio range measurements. We show that the precision of current range measurements can probe ultralight dark matter at masses around $10^{-15}\,$eV, had its density in the solar system been $10^5$ larger than the so-called local dark matter density. This limit complements other constraints, such as the one from analyses of pulsar timing observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.20689.title: Gravitational Wave Birefringence in generalized Palatini Chern Simons
arxiv.org/abs/2607.20689.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.20689v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The cosmological propagation of gravitational waves (GWs) can exhibit amplitude and phase polarization distortions when parity symmetry is broken, a phenomenon known as cosmological birefringence. In this paper, we investigate the phenomenology of GW birefringence in a gravitational model $f(R)$ coupled to a dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) term, analyzed in the metric and Palatini formalisms. At the background level, this model can lead to dynamical dark energy, while for GW propagation we find that the Palatini formalism predicts both amplitude and velocity birefringence, whereas the metric formalism predicts amplitude birefringence only. We also find that the birefringence effects can either be suppressed or enhanced by the $f(R)$ interactions, depending on the specific form of $f(R)$. Considering three common $f(R)$ models (Hu-Sawicki, Exponential, and Hyperbolic gravity) fit to recent cosmological data, we find that birefringence is enhanced relative to the $f(R) = R$ case, by $1-10\%$ in the Palatini formalism and up to a factor of 2 in the metric formalism. We also translate current GW birefringence constraints to bounds on the dCS coupling within our model. Finally, we show that in our model the birefringence effect grows polynomially with source redshift, in contrast to the linear-distance scaling commonly assumed in phenomenological models of GW birefringence in the current literature.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.34338.title: Neutron star cooling with medium-modified Urca rates
arxiv.org/abs/2609.34338.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.34338v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study the effects of in-medium modification of the elementary cooling processes on observable properties of isolated neutron stars. We deduce the neutron star mass distributions compatible with the cooling analysis and compare with current theoretical models. We conclude that current cooling data require fast direct Urca cooling, moderated by proton superfluidity, to be active in most neutron stars, and that the DU onset threshold must lie below canonical masses. In that case medium modifications of modified Urca rates are practically insignificant, but the nn Bremsstrahlung rate plays a dominant role.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.14129.title: IceCube data for astrophysical neutrinos exhibit q-statistical behavior
arxiv.org/abs/2610.14129.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.14129v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Relevant IceCube recent data for astrophysical neutrinos are analyzed. Similarly to cosmic rays and proton-proton LHC collisions, the corresponding spectra are satisfactorily described, for the entire interval of measured energies, through $q$-Gaussians. This fact reinforces the already available evidence that nonadditive entropies (either of the $S_q$ class or of the $S_\delta$ one, or even alternative ones) appear to play a crucial role in systems such as black holes and related cosmological phenomena (e.g., dark energy). The IceCube data yield high values for the momenta-distribution nonadditive index ($q \simeq 1.6$, hence $q_{energy} \simeq 1.3$), to be compared with the cosmic rays values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.2$) and the LHC values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.1$). This fact neatly indicates very-long-ranged space-time correlations. The detailed associated physical mechanisms remain, at the present stage, as an instigating open issue.

universetoday.com/articles/interstellar-.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
universetoday.com/articles/interstellar-.excerpt: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.

phys.org/news/2026-11-plastic-bags-bottl.title: Plastic bags and bottles become industrial-strength adhesives through new upcycling method
phys.org/news/2026-11-plastic-bags-bottl.excerpt: Around 450 million metric tons of plastics are produced worldwide each year. The major share of this sheer volume is used only once and then winds up in an incinerator or in landfills. This also applies to so-called polyolefins, which include polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP). As packaging materials and films, they account for approximately half of our plastic consumption.

phys.org/news/2026-11-empathy-joyful-sto.title: New tests expand empathy measurement to joyful stories and embarrassing mishaps
phys.org/news/2026-11-empathy-joyful-sto.excerpt: Listening to someone recount their visit to an amusement park can feel like being on an emotional roller coaster yourself. Even if the listeners have never set foot in the park, they can still empathize with the other person's feelings: the deep disappointment when it turns out that their favorite ride is closed. The joy—at having the best ice cream of their life. And the embarrassment—after that ice cream abruptly left their stomach on the Freefall Tower. Put simply: whatever the other person is feeling, we feel it with them.

phys.org/news/2026-11-black-characters-s.title: Black characters receive similar precision ratings whether they look 'nerdy' or 'chill'
phys.org/news/2026-11-black-characters-s.excerpt: People are often asked simple questions, such as the price of the cheapest flight to a particular destination. But the answers—and how they are perceived—can reveal far more than the cost of that trip itself. For example, whether a person believes that the response "It's $200" means $200 or assumes that the figure has been rounded up or down depends on their perception of the person giving the answer.

phys.org/news/2026-11-artificial-intelli.title: Connecting artificial intelligence with the tools of astrophysical research
phys.org/news/2026-11-artificial-intelli.excerpt: Investigating a scientific question is often a complex process. As an astrophysicist studying some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe, I know that finding answers requires much more than reading scientific papers or understanding existing theories. Astrophysical research involves collecting observations, analyzing data, building physical models and comparing their predictions with observations. These tasks require different scientific tools, databases and modeling software and can take considerable time even for experienced researchers.

phys.org/news/2026-11-electrical-unconve.title: Electrical control of an unconventional quantum transport state demonstrated in a magnet for the first time
phys.org/news/2026-11-electrical-unconve.excerpt: Researchers at Tohoku University and the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) have successfully controlled a unique quantum phenomenon—the quantum-geometric nonlinear Hall (QgNLH) state—using electric current for the first time. The breakthrough was achieved by revealing and exploiting the coupling between the spin structure and the QgNLH state in an electrically switchable chiral antiferromagnet.

phys.org/news/2026-11-palm-characteristi.title: How palm orientation shapes spin characteristics in volleyball jump serves
phys.org/news/2026-11-palm-characteristi.excerpt: A new biomechanical study has uncovered how elite volleyball players control ball spin during jump serves, offering fresh scientific insight into one of the sport's most decisive offensive skills.

phys.org/news/2026-11-physicist-detector.title: Physicist develops detector capable of counting photons for quantum computing
phys.org/news/2026-11-physicist-detector.excerpt: Detecting a single photon is a challenge in itself. But what if you also want to know exactly how many photons arrive at a particular point at the same time? Physicist Erik Baalbergen is working on light detectors that can do just that. They form a key building block for the optical quantum computer of the future.

phys.org/news/2026-11-citizen-science-ex.title: Citizen science program helps find exotic ticks
phys.org/news/2026-11-citizen-science-ex.excerpt: Climate change is affecting not only our weather but also the distribution of parasites and the diseases they can carry. One example is the growing presence of Hyalomma ticks in parts of Europe where they were previously uncommon. These ticks are of particular interest because they can transmit Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), a pathogen that can cause serious, sometimes life-threatening illness in humans. Hyalomma ticks are typically found in warm and dry regions of Africa, Asia and southern Europe. However, they have increasingly been reported farther north, including in Central Europe.

phys.org/news/2026-11-antarctic-blue-wha.title: As Antarctic blue whales advance along the road to recovery, continued oversight is key
phys.org/news/2026-11-antarctic-blue-wha.excerpt: Antarctic blue whales appear to be creeping back from the brink of extinction after 50 years of protection. A new study estimates the total population at 4,018, up from 418 after the last reported whale catch in 1973.

phys.org/news/2026-11-octopuses-small-ga.title: How octopuses squeeze through too-small gaps
phys.org/news/2026-11-octopuses-small-ga.excerpt: Octopuses are extraordinarily versatile. From walking across the seabed on their eight arms to jetting through the water, manipulating tools and squeezing through unimaginably tight spaces, the flexibility of octopuses almost defies belief. "Octopuses can change their body shape to squeeze through tiny holes, almost like water flowing through a gap, so their size doesn't always limit where they can go," says Wenci Xin from the National University of Singapore.

phys.org/news/2026-11-born-queen-ant-hie.title: Born to be queen: A look inside fire ant hierarchy
phys.org/news/2026-11-born-queen-ant-hie.excerpt: A group of genes may give some fire ants an advantage, increasing their chances of growing larger and potentially becoming queens, according to a new study from the University of Georgia.

phys.org/news/2026-11-private-schools-se.title: How private schools segregate students by class and strengthen social divisions
phys.org/news/2026-11-private-schools-se.excerpt: If you want to see how private schools in the U.K. can reinforce segregation between children of different social classes, the London Borough of Southwark provides a good example.

phys.org/news/2026-11-avian-influenza-ba.title: Avian influenza spread beyond a backyard coop on an Illinois farm, analysis finds
phys.org/news/2026-11-avian-influenza-ba.excerpt: An outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus that nearly wiped out an Illinois farmer's backyard flock also spread to a domestic cat and wild rats on the farm, an analysis of the animals by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory and the University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory found.

phys.org/news/2026-11-newly-protein-mech.title: Newly identified protein mechanism helps explain how cells respond to physical forces
phys.org/news/2026-11-newly-protein-mech.excerpt: A newly published study is changing our understanding of how the protein talin functions at sites where cells attach to their surroundings. The findings uncover a previously unknown mechanism by which mechanical force regulates talin, a key protein controlling cell adhesion and mechanosensing. The paper is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys.org/news/2026-11-bed-psychology-sea.title: Clothes on the bed, nothing feels right: The psychology behind your seasonal wardrobe meltdown
phys.org/news/2026-11-bed-psychology-sea.excerpt: The clocks have gone back, and suddenly getting dressed feels more difficult. The coat you wore constantly last winter is still hanging in the closet, but it no longer looks quite how you remember. The boots you loved in February don't seem to go with anything, while a sweater that once felt like you somehow doesn't anymore.

phys.org/news/2026-11-hubble-galactic-hi.title: Hubble learns galactic history from stars
phys.org/news/2026-11-hubble-galactic-hi.excerpt: This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image provides a lesson in galactic history. The sparkling collection of stars is named Messier 30 (M30) after the French astronomer Charles Messier, who cataloged M30 and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets in the early telescopes of Messier's time. M30 lies about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus.

phys.org/news/2026-11-microscopy-method-.title: New microscopy method reveals tiny cell structures and their molecular surroundings
phys.org/news/2026-11-microscopy-method-.excerpt: How do cells respond to drugs? A new microscopy technique could provide more precise answers to this question in the future. Researchers from Bielefeld University and the University of Vienna have developed a method as part of the European CHEM-SCAN project that makes the smallest cellular structures visible while also showing how their molecular environment changes.

phys.org/news/2026-11-linguist-magic-son.title: Linguist to record the magic songs of the Awajún people of Peru
phys.org/news/2026-11-linguist-magic-son.excerpt: There is magic in the traditional songs of the Awajún, an Indigenous people of northern Peruvian Amazonia. Otago linguist Dr. Simon Overall has been visiting this area for over 20 years and explains what gives these songs their powers.

phys.org/news/2026-11-chilean-rodent-pop.title: Chilean rodent population collapse reveals how extreme drought can overwhelm wildlife's resilience
phys.org/news/2026-11-chilean-rodent-pop.excerpt: Research published in the journal Ecology analyzed 12 years of records from a population of degus in central Chile, revealing that these endemic rodents managed to withstand nearly a decade of megadrought but disappeared locally following the extreme drought of 2019.

phys.org/news/2026-11-ancient-maya-mercu.title: Ancient Maya mercury use may have come at a severe environmental cost
phys.org/news/2026-11-ancient-maya-mercu.excerpt: Ancient Maya communities made extensive use of liquid mercury and a red, mercury-containing pigment called cinnabar to decorate buildings, pottery and burial sites. Unsurprisingly, as previous research has shown, this led to mercury contamination of soils and reservoirs at some Maya sites. And that pollution may have spread even farther into their territory and caused the collapse of two lake ecosystems, according to a study published in the journal Science Advances.

phys.org/news/2026-11-synergistic-additi.title: Researchers develop synergistic additives for scalable slot-die-coated perovskite photovoltaics
phys.org/news/2026-11-synergistic-additi.excerpt: A research team led by Professor Yang Dong from the Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics (DICP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with Dalian Jiaotong University, has developed a synergistic additive strategy for large-area slot-die coating of methylammonium-free (MA-free) perovskite films. The study is published in Advanced Materials.

phys.org/news/2026-11-ice-age-abrupt-cli.title: Ice-age abrupt climate shifts were not as fast as thought, new study finds
phys.org/news/2026-11-ice-age-abrupt-cli.excerpt: New high-resolution speleothem records from China and India, together with isotope-enabled climate models, show that abrupt glacial ocean circulation recoveries took centuries, not decades—a finding with important implications for how we assess future Atlantic circulation change. The work is published in the journal Science.

phys.org/news/2026-11-based-hair-dye-cin.title: A plant-based hair dye that smells like cinnamon
phys.org/news/2026-11-based-hair-dye-cin.excerpt: Hair dyes help people express style and cover gray hair but often contain skin-irritating chemicals.

phys.org/news/2026-11-hooved-mammals-mig.title: Hooved mammals that migrate may be at greater risk of extinction than those that stay put
phys.org/news/2026-11-hooved-mammals-mig.excerpt: Over the past 100,000 years, hooved mammals that migrate have experienced a higher rate of extinction compared to nonmigratory species, according to a study being published Nov. 5 in the journal PLOS Biology by Joel Abraham at Princeton University, U.S., and colleagues.

phys.org/news/2026-11-cannabis-intoxican.title: Cannabis was used as an intoxicant as early as 2,800 years ago
phys.org/news/2026-11-cannabis-intoxican.excerpt: Cannabis is one of the most commonly used psychoactive plants today. However, it is difficult to determine archaeologically how cannabis was used in prehistoric times. Plant parts such as flowers, leaves and resins are perishable and therefore rarely survive. It is known that cannabis served various purposes, such as the production of oil or fiber, and was not used solely as medicine or a drug.

phys.org/news/2026-11-dna-nanoswitches-d.title: DNA nanoswitches find new drug leads faster by measuring protein interactions
phys.org/news/2026-11-dna-nanoswitches-d.excerpt: Researchers at the Wyss Institute at Harvard University, Boston Children's Hospital, and Harvard Medical School (HMS) have developed FIND, a drug discovery platform that searches large libraries for molecules that modulate binding interactions between two proteins. FIND uses DNA nanoswitches to select drug candidates based on their effects on these protein-protein interactions, rather than simply whether they bind to a single target protein, giving it a key advantage over conventional binding-based screening.

phys.org/news/2026-11-blocking-specific-.title: Blocking specific molecular signal on immune cells may restore ability to fight mutated cells
phys.org/news/2026-11-blocking-specific-.excerpt: A previously unrecognized weakness in the immune defenses against certain blood neoplasms could offer a promising target for future treatments. Researchers have discovered that natural killer cells, which normally help the body eliminate malignant cells, remain remarkably active in patients with a particular genetic form of blood neoplasms. However, their ability to fight the disease appears to be restricted by an inhibitory molecular signal.

phys.org/news/2026-11-molecular-helicity.title: Controlling molecular helicity: A new approach to constructing chiral nanographenes
phys.org/news/2026-11-molecular-helicity.excerpt: Nanographenes with up to eight helicene units can now be selectively synthesized using a two-step process. Researchers from Science Tokyo have developed a strategy to synthesize multi-helical nanographenes containing up to eight helicene units with controlled handedness.

phys.org/news/2026-11-explore-ai-earthqu.title: Researchers explore how AI could improve earthquake safety
phys.org/news/2026-11-explore-ai-earthqu.excerpt: Researchers at the University of East London (UEL) have developed a new framework for assessing earthquake risks, using AI-assisted technology to examine how soil conditions, ground shaking and structural strength influence a building's ability to withstand seismic activity.

phys.org/news/2026-11-a-well-timed-blink.title: A well-timed blink helps us to look around
phys.org/news/2026-11-a-well-timed-blink.excerpt: When did you last blink? Every few seconds, we briefly close our eyes, interrupting our view of the world. Most of the time, we do not notice. What is more, these brief interruptions hardly seem to interfere with our everyday activities.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.06963.title: Unveiling the Origins of Local Group Galaxies with ELT-SHARP: An Overview of Science Cases
arxiv.org/abs/2611.06963.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.06963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The $\Lambda$CDM paradigm successfully describes large-scale cosmic structure, yet tensions possibly persist on galactic and sub-galactic scales. The Milky Way and the Local Universe offer a uniquely accessible laboratory to probe these discrepancies through chemo-dynamical studies of resolved stellar populations. Understanding disk assembly, dynamical heating, and galactoseismology requires wide-field coverage and high-angular-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy capable of penetrating dust-obscured regions and resolving crowded stellar environments. We propose science cases exploiting \textsc{SHARP}, a multi-mode near-infrared spectrograph for Extremely Large Telescopes and future space facilities. Operating over $0.95$--$2.45\,\mu$m in a single exposure, \textsc{SHARP} enables efficient access to key stellar and gas tracers across the Galactic bulge, disk, halo, and nearby galaxies. The \textsc{NEXUS} mode provides adaptive-optics-assisted multi-object spectroscopy over a $1.2'\times1.2'$ field with spectral resolutions up to $R\sim17{,}000$, enabling gas and stellar kinematics. Complementarily, the \textsc{VESPER} multi-IFU mode delivers spatially resolved spectroscopy in crowded regions, allowing reconstruction of internal kinematics and stellar population gradients on sub-arcsecond scales. Combined with surveys such as \textit{Gaia}, APOGEE, LAMOST, LSST, 4MOST, and ELT--MOSAIC, this project will map six-dimensional phase-space structures of disk and bulge stars, stellar streams, and nearby disk galaxies (e.g. LMC, SMC). The data will enable investigations of bars, spiral arms, warps, flares, and satellite interactions, providing critical constraints on disk evolution, merger history, and dark matter substructure, and providing stringent tests of $\Lambda$CDM on the smallest accessible scales.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.06966.title: SHARP(ening the) view of unresolved globular clusters in ultra diffuse galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2611.06966.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.06966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs) challenge current galaxy formation models within the {\Lambda}CDM framework, particularly regarding their dark matter content and formation histories. Globular Clusters (GCs) serve as excellent tracers for probing the halos of these faint systems; however, current spectroscopic facilities struggle to reach the depth required to fully characterize GC populations beyond the local neighborhood. In this work, we present the scientific potential of NEXUS@SHARP, a near-infrared multi-slit spectrograph proposed on the upcoming Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). We demonstrate that NEXUS is uniquely positioned to overcome current observational limitations by combining high spatial resolution with efficient multiplexing. We show that NEXUS can efficiently help to characterize the GC population in UDGs across diverse environments out to 60 to 70 Mpc - with a few hours of ELT time. These capabilities will allow for precise measurements of radial velocities and stellar populations, enabling robust dynamical mass estimates and distinguishing between competing UDG formation scenario.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.07006.title: Black Hole Seeds and Little Red Dots: Connecting Formation and Growth with a JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Program
arxiv.org/abs/2611.07006.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.07006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: JWST has revealed an abundant population of faint active galactic nuclei and a new class of compact, high-redshift sources known as Little Red Dots (LRDs), whose physical nature remains debated, with accreting massive black holes among the leading explanations. The emerging demographics of early black holes, with their high inferred number densities and, in some systems, the apparent excess of black hole mass relative to stellar mass, challenge simple scenarios of black hole seeding and growth. Despite these observational breakthroughs, the origin of early massive black holes remains uncertain, because "black holes have no memory": current samples cannot separate the imprint of seeding from subsequent growth. This white paper identifies the multi-cycle JWST observations needed to revolutionize our understanding of early black hole growth by: (i) distinguishing seeding pathways, (ii) constraining early black hole growth mechanisms, (iii) resolving the physical nature of broad-line emitters and LRDs, and (iv) testing black hole-galaxy co-evolution.
