The caustic analysis reveals distinct topological regimes, Sgr A* retains both tangential and radial critical curves, while M87* may show only tangential critical curves due to its larger mass. This topological difference provides a clear observational signature for future observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.22080.title: [CII] as a global cold gas tracer in novel hydrodynamical simulations
arxiv.org/abs/2608.22080.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.22080v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: [CII] emission is a powerful tool for studying the gas content in galaxies, especially at early stages of evolution. Given its low excitation potential, the [CII] 158 \mu m line is the main coolant of neutral gas in photodissociation regions and giant molecular clouds, hence a tracer of all phases of the interstellar medium. However, there is no consensus on what is the nature of the gas traced by this emission. We aim to provide insights into the physics of the [CII] emission and predictions for future observations. We used four pre-prepared simulations performed with a version of p-gadget-3, which includes the krome chemistry package. We implemented a postprocessing semi-analytical model to simulate the [CII] emission. We analysed an isolated Milky Way-mass-size galaxy, and three merger configurations: a co-rotating, counter-rotating, and perpendicular major mergers of two Milky Way-mass-size galaxies. We reproduce fundamental relations such as the [CII] luminosity and the star formation rate, L[CII]-SFR relation, in which mergers show an extra component for the [CII] emission not traced by the star formation alone. During quiescent or starburst stages, galaxies deviate from the L[CII]-SFR relation. We find that [CII] is a robust tracer of molecular gas, as well as atomic gas in both cold and warm phases on a global scale. Our results indicate that around 50 per cent of the total [CII] emission is traced by molecular gas, while 30 to 40 per cent is traced by atomic and ionised hydrogen regardless of the configuration. Our findings suggest that the nature of the [CII] emission depends strongly on the evolutionary history of galaxies, in which mergers and starbursts act as more efficient drivers of [CII] emission through collision with molecular hydrogen.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.24873.title: Magnesium silicate condensation in sub-Neptune envelopes: the fundamental link between chemistry, structure, and observables
arxiv.org/abs/2608.24873.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.24873v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Chemical interactions between the hydrogen-dominated envelopes and silicate-rich interiors of sub-Neptunes likely play a key role in shaping their atmospheric structure, mass-radius relations, and upper atmosphere composition. While atmospheric abundances and structure deeply influence each other, many existing models have either considered the effects of chemical interactions without the structural implications or have modeled the envelope structure using oversimplified chemical networks. In this work, we introduce Rocky Raccoon, a coupled chemical equilibrium-atmospheric structure model. This model incorporates Mg, Si, O, C, and H species and produces self-consistent atmospheric chemical and thermal profiles for sub-Neptune envelopes, treating multi-species condensation for the first time. We find that the condensation sequence of magnesium silicates above a magma ocean is determined by the basal magma composition. We show that these condensation sequences drive the upper atmospheric composition to two endmembers: high oxygen abundances in the underlying melt produce compositions rich in oxygen-bearing volatiles (sub-solar C/O) and higher mean molecular weight atmospheres with $\mu \sim 4$ amu, while oxygen-poor melts produce lower mean molecular weight atmospheres dominated by methane and silane (super-solar C/O). The transition between the two regimes is abrupt and depends on melt properties like Mg/Si ratios and oxygen abundances. The different condensation sequences also lead to different thermal profiles, as deep convection is inhibited over different regions due to varying molecular weight gradients. Further experiments and simulations are key to resolving critical uncertainties in the condensation sequences and the corresponding significant impacts on sub-Neptune composition and thermal structure.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.07792.title: Filament-Arm Node Systems (FANS): A new probe of the winding and chirality of the cosmic web
arxiv.org/abs/2609.07792.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.07792v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We define Filament-Arm Node Systems (FANS), a new class of cosmic-web objects consisting of multiple filament arms connected to a common node, and use their geometry to construct an object-based test of cosmic chirality. With the cosmic-web node providing a natural reference point, FANS span characteristic scales of ~60 Mpc/h, allowing the coherent winding of their arms around the node to be measured directly. We define cosmic spirality as the amplitude of this winding and handedness as its signed clockwise (CW) or counter-clockwise (CCW) sense. We further introduce an axis-conditioned extrinsic estimator that searches for the projected signature of a coherent three-dimensional axial pattern of the handedness field, corresponding to a preferred axis of winding. Applying these measurements to two distinct SDSS filament reconstructions, and assessing their significance with sign-flip nulls and 27 controlled variations of the FANS construction parameters, we find no significant preference for CW or CCW winding, either globally or around a preferred axis. The data are therefore consistent with parity symmetry, as expected in standard LCDM cosmology. Comparing the lowest- and highest-redshift bins over 0.1<0.6, we find that cosmic spirality decreases with cosmic time, a trend that also persists within individual arm-multiplicity classes and may reflect the gravitational straightening of filament arms. These first constraints establish FANS as a new probe of cosmic-web symmetry and large-scale morphology and provide a baseline for future parity tests with the much larger filament samples expected from upcoming surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.22432.title: A Quantitative Method to Investigate the Spectral Class Time Evolution of Novae
arxiv.org/abs/2609.22432.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.22432v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Novae are spectroscopically classified as Fe II or He/N according to the dominance of Fe II, or He and N emission lines in their pre-nebular spectra, while spectra exhibiting both are classified as hybrid. Whereas the spectral class of a nova is known to correlate with its progenitor properties, a recent detailed spectroscopic follow-up of ten novae suggests instead a time evolution from "early He/N" to "Fe II" and to "late He/N". We investigate here this apparent contradiction using a spectroscopic dataset of 26 novae from the Astronomical Ring for Amateur Spectroscopy (ARAS) Database. For this purpose we introduce a quantitative coefficient, $\kappa$, defined as the ratio of the flux of the Fe II $\lambda$5169 line to the mean flux of five He and N emission lines, with $\kappa > 1$ indicating Fe II-dominated spectra and $\kappa < 1$ indicating He/N-dominated spectra. This coefficient is shown to provide a reliable quantitative tool for tracing nova spectral evolution while reducing biases from incomplete coverage. A significant fraction of the novae in our sample exhibit at least one transition between Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases. The time evolution of $\kappa$ closely follows their optical light-curves, repeatedly crossing unity in novae exhibiting jitters, which reveal non-monotonic spectral evolution. Since the light-curve shapes and their time-scales depend on intrinsic progenitor properties, particularly white dwarf mass, they also determine the duration of Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases, introducing a bias in spectral classification when it relies on early, sparse spectra.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.25810.title: A Brief Review on the Statistical Properties of Fast Radio Bursts
arxiv.org/abs/2609.25810.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.25810v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin, whose emission mechanisms and progenitors remain unresolved. Statistical analyses of the rapidly growing samples provide a promising means to constrain the underlying physics. In this review, we synthesize the statistical properties derived from current FRB catalogs, encompassing constraints on dispersion measure, redshift, energy/luminosity functions, repetition rate, and host-galaxy demographics. For repeating FRBs, we examine the statistics of energy, fluence/flux, waiting time, and discuss time-series analyses that reveal memory effects and chaotic dynamics. We further discuss the observational discovery and theoretical interpretation of periodic activity, and survey polarization properties that probe the magneto-ionic environments of FRB sources. Throughout, we emphasize robust empirical trends, account for observational biases and selection effects, and outline outstanding open questions regarding the physical origin of these enigmatic bursts.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.26683.title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images
arxiv.org/abs/2609.26683.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.26683v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Accurately predicting fast solar wind conditions is challenging, as uncertainties are large and unquantified by traditional single-value prediction models. In particular, the risks of high-speed solar wind streams (HSSs), which can cause damage to technological infrastructure, cannot be reliably assessed without probabilistic forecasts. We present PROSWIN, a probabilistic machine learning model that forecasts the hourly solar wind speed (SWS) at Earth with a four-day lead time. The approach combines solar images and magnetograms using a deep neural network coupled to a distributional regression algorithm. Because standard error metrics underweight the relevance of HSS peaks, we further introduce the prediction score, a model-selection metric that jointly rewards timeline and HSS peak accuracy. On 14 years of data, our forecast achieves very well-calibrated uncertainties (<1% average deviation). Using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), a metric that assesses distributional accuracy, we obtain a timeline CRPS of 41.0 km/s, an HSS peak CRPS of 45.3 km/s, and a prediction score of 42.3 km/s. We find that the 171 {\AA} channel is an important complement to the typically used 193 {\AA} and 211 {\AA} channels and that the prediction score for model selection improves the applicability of the model. Compared to selected models from the literature, ours is the only one that is accurate for both timeline and HSS peak values, rather than trading one off against the other. These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single-value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.35471.title: Diverse Metallicities in Protoclusters at $z \sim 3.4$ detected by Deep Learning
arxiv.org/abs/2609.35471.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.35471v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present spectroscopic follow-up observations with Subaru/MOIRCS of four protocluster candidate regions identified by the deep-learning model PCFNet. In three candidate regions, we confirm four protoclusters at $z =$ 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, exhibiting galaxy density peaks over five times the uniform distribution. The detection rate of confirmed members aligns with PCFNet's predictions, underscoring its effectiveness. Analysis of spectral energy distributions (SEDs), incorporating up to ten photometric bands $(uu^*grizyJHK)$, reveals that protocluster members lie on the star-formation main sequence. The masses of the most massive halos in the protoclusters are estimated from the most massive stellar mass of the member galaxies, yielding $\log M_\mathrm{halo}/M_\odot=12.4$-$12.8$, which are consistent with those at this redshift predicted by cosmological simulations and are comparable to those of the progenitors of typical local clusters ($M_\mathrm{halo}^{z=0}\sim10^{14}M_\odot$). Using the Voronoi Tessellation Monte Carlo technique based on the probability of protocluster membership from PCFNet, we find that our protoclusters exhibit a significantly higher SFRD than the cosmic SFRD at $z\sim3.4$. Based on the [Oiii]/H$\beta$ emission line ratio, two protoclusters show marginally ($1.4$-$2\sigma$) higher average metallicities than the field, while the other protoclusters are statistically consistent with the field. These diverse metallicities highlight the environmental impact within protoclusters detected by PCFNet, likely reflecting the complex opposing interplay between metal-rich gas recycling and metal-poor gas inflow, which may depend on the surrounding environment of each protocluster. This work demonstrates PCFNet's capability to unveil diverse samples of high-redshift protoclusters, paving the way for a more comprehensive understanding of their role in galaxy evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.07244.title: Lensing in the Blue IV: The First Weak Gravitational Lensing Maps from the Stratosphere
arxiv.org/abs/2610.07244.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.07244v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Super-Pressure Balloon-borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT) completed its science flight in April 2023, obtaining imaging data for 30 galaxy clusters. In this work, we present the first weak-lensing convergence maps from these observations, using six clusters selected from the 30 targets. We construct background-galaxy catalogs using SuperBIT's three-band photometry and a color-color-based method to separate foreground and background galaxies. Using the calibrated shapes of the selected background galaxies, we reconstruct the weak-lensing convergence field through Kaiser--Squires inversion. We compare the convergence signal-to-noise maps for the six clusters with independent tracers of the mass distribution, namely, red-sequence cluster-member number density maps. These results demonstrate the first successful reconstruction of a weak-lensing signal using imaging data from a sub-orbital astronomical observatory.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.07421.title: Axial-Dipole and Equatorial-Dipole Coronal Holes: Congruent Magnetic Geometry, Divergent Evolution
arxiv.org/abs/2610.07421.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.07421v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While the Sun's polar fields reverse, the axial dipole is weak and low-latitude coronal holes are common. Where the equatorial dipole is strong, these holes form at its magnetic poles, as the axial-dipole coronal holes (ADCHs) of solar minimum form at the poles of the axial dipole; we call them equatorial-dipole coronal holes (EDCHs). Not every low-latitude hole is an EDCH: in 2024 August, near maximum, the quadrupole and higher multipoles led the field. Parker Solar Probe found fast wind from an EDCH deeply sub-Alfv\'enic at $9.9\,R_\odot$, at only $60\%$ of an asymptotic speed equal to that of polar wind, which is thought to accelerate faster. We ask whether coronal structure predicts this, using potential-field models of synthetic and observed fields. Pure axial and equatorial dipoles are exactly congruent, so any difference between the two classes must come from their orientation relative to differential rotation or from the surrounding multipoles. ADCHs are stationary and sustained by converging meridional flow. EDCHs depend on an equatorial dipole that active-region emergence builds and flux transport removes: over $18$-day sequences the axial dipole at minimum is steady to $1\%$, whereas the equatorial dipole varies by $21\%$ at maximum and $8\%$ in the declining phase. Most open flux in EDCHs expands less than in ADCHs, and their boundaries are dominated by pseudostreamers with non-monotonic expansion. Magnetic geometry alone does not predict slower acceleration from EDCHs; a real difference would point to extended heating by Alfv\'en-wave turbulence, which potential-field models cannot capture.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.08728.title: When, Why, and How CMB Compression Fails
arxiv.org/abs/2610.08728.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.08728v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We test when compressed CMB likelihoods can be reliably used to constrain new physics beyond $\Lambda$CDM, formulating concrete criteria for when, why, and how CMB compression fails. We derive our conclusions by exploring a broad set of models that modify different aspects of the cosmological evolution, including late-time dark-energy dynamics, non-standard late-time dark-matter evolution through interactions or decay, and dark-matter models with persistently non-standard redshift evolution. For each case, we compare the results obtained from data combinations based on the full Planck-CMB likelihood with their counterparts based on a compressed CMB likelihood calibrated in $\Lambda$CDM. We find that the compression remains accurate for late-time dark-energy extensions that preserve the dark-matter background evolution and do not introduce significant additional perturbative effects. By contrast, modifying the dark-matter evolution breaks the mapping between the present-day matter density and the matter density at the epochs relevant to the CMB, causing the compressed constraints to fail even when the modification acts exclusively at late times. In these cases, the compressed likelihood can drastically alter the geometry of the multidimensional posterior distributions, shifting their centers, producing strongly anisotropic deformations, reordering principal modes, and generating genuine mixing and rotation of their eigendirections. These multidimensional distortions propagate into substantially incorrect marginalized constraints on cosmological parameters, with differences between the full and compressed analyses reaching nearly an order of magnitude in some of the cases studied here.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13742.title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous $z>2$ quasars
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13742.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13742v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We aim to provide a cookbook for purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and to provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous $z>2$ quasars. We analyse the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. We show that the proper motion signal to noise $\mu/\sigma_{\mu}$ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking into account the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopt the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled $\chi^2$ distribution with $k=2$ and scale $s=1.1485$ is fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding $\pm2\sigma$ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is $D^2_{M(\mu)}<7.097$. The final criteria combine this with the parallax condition and $\mathrm{ruwe}<1.4$. Applying the new criteria to the SDSS DR16Q confirmed quasars, the recovery rate is $90.25\%$. The suggested purely astrometric selection significantly improves both completeness and purity compared to other strategies used in the literature, reaching a quasar purity of approximately $95\%$ ($\sim2\sigma$ Gaussian-equivalent). It can be used to improve the selection purity and completeness for future quasar surveys. As an example, we use the suggested strategi to locate 24 very bright $z>2$ quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95\% of known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries is demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous $z>2$ quasars. Ten of these are new discoveries and for an additional seven we correct the redshifts determined by other methods.}

arxiv.org/abs/2610.22239.title: High-frequency water megamasers as precision probes of black holes, galaxies and cosmology: A case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer
arxiv.org/abs/2610.22239.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.22239v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Water megamasers in the circumnuclear disks of active galactic nuclei are among the most precise probes of supermassive black holes. VLBI imaging of 22 GHz disk masers has provided geometric distances to independently constrain $H_0$, accurate black hole mass measurements, and sub-parsec views of accretion disk geometry. ALMA has opened a new window into water maser transitions in the sub-mm/mm regime, which trace temperatures, densities and disk regions that are inaccessible at 22 GHz, and can be observed at higher spatial resolution and with less free-free absorption. However, current detections are limited to a few bright extragalactic masers in nearby galaxies. We present the case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer - ALMA2040 - that would open a new parameter space for maser studies. We show that a 10-fold increase in line sensitivity and three times longer baselines compared to ALMA would transform sub-mm maser studies from a few bright detections into a population-level probe, delivering black hole masses and geometric distances from sub-mm masers alone, independent of and complementary to 22 GHz measurements. Integrated into a VLBI array, ALMA2040 would resolve maser disks out to $>$160 Mpc, extend maser black hole masses into the largely untested intermediate-mass regime, reveal magnetic field structure in accretion disks through polarization studies, and test systematics in $H_0$ measurements.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.22804.title: Gaia in Technicolor. I. A Simple Variability-Encoded Color-Magnitude Diagram
arxiv.org/abs/2610.22804.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.22804v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is one of the most important tools in stellar astrophysics. In its modern, empirical form as the Gaia color-magnitude diagram (CMD), each star is represented with a point determined from its time-averaged brightness and color. However, many stars are intrinsically variable, and the fixed-point representation ignores the variety of ways in which a star can vary. As a system pulsates, eclipses, is irradiated, erupts, or otherwise varies, it moves through the CMD along a trajectory whose size, slope, and shape are determined by the physics driving the brightness and color variability. Here we exploit the near-simultaneous, three-band, multi-epoch photometry (MEP) released for ~11.7 million sources in Gaia DR3 to construct a variability-encoded CMD (VECMD). In this updated take on the traditional CMD, each star is represented not by a point but by a linear segment approximating the path it traces in absolute magnitude and color as it varies. Because these trajectories are built from the raw epoch data, they are agnostic to period and do not require phase-folding. We show that radial-mode pulsators trace looped, Lissajous-like trajectories that can encode the phase lag between radius and temperature. The Hertzsprung bump is even visible in the CMD loops of some Cepheids. Variable binary systems can trace tight color-correlated lines and/or hooked paths. Accreting and dust-obscured systems trace long, high-amplitude tracks aligned with the outburst or reddening vector. Distinct regions of the VECMD are dominated by distinct trajectory morphologies. We argue that these trajectories are period-independent fingerprints well suited to machine learning classification, which we will pursue on the much larger epoch-photometry sample expected in Gaia DR4. Finally, we present a free app called IVECMD for finding, classifying, and analyzing variable stars in the VECMD.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.24195.title: Modeling Multi-band Active Galactic Nuclei Lightcurves Using a Self-supervised Attentive Neural Process Network
arxiv.org/abs/2610.24195.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.24195v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: With the the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), observations of tens of millions of quasars are expected. We present a machine-learning framework based on an attentive neural process (ANP) that models stochastic quasar variability and jointly performs two tasks: (i) probabilistic reconstruction of quasar light curves in all six LSST bands, and (ii) inference of physical parameters of the AGN system --- black hole mass, Eddington ratio, and intrinsic variability timescale --- with joint, full-covariance posteriors. The model processes all six bands within a single masked attention mechanism, so that observations in any band constrain the shared driving process, and natively handles irregularly and asynchronously sampled light curves with realistic heteroscedastic noise. We train and evaluate on full ten-year light curves simulated with a relativistic accretion-disk reprocessing model, observed through the fielded Rubin baseline cadence with per-visit photometric noise. The light-curve model is trained with self-supervised, learning from the sparse noisy observations alone and never accessing the underlying noiseless light curves. On a held-out test set, we show that our ANP model reach comparable performances to that of the near-optimal baseline Gaussian process model, while exceeding it in power spectrum reconstruction and damped-random walk timescale estimation. The compact learned latent representation supports future downstream applications, and the fully observation-driven training objective enables direct fine-tuning on real LSST light curves.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.29610.title: OGLE-2013-BLG-1125/MOA-2013-BLG-584: Discovery of a gas giant orbiting an M dwarf
arxiv.org/abs/2610.29610.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.29610v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We report the discovery and characterization of a planetary system in the microlensing event OGLE-2013-BLG-1125/MOA-2013-BLG-584. We analyze photometric data from OGLE and MOA surveys, as well as LCO, $\mu$FUN, and Mindstep follow-up telescopes to model the microlensing light curve. We also used data from the Keck II telescope collected in 2018 to obtain additional constraints on the lensing system. We found a Saturn-mass planet of mass $M_{\rm p}=105\pm13 \ M_\oplus$ orbiting a low-mass host star $M_{\rm L}=0.139\pm0.011 \ M_\odot$ at $1.00\pm0.08$ kpc from Earth. This discovery adds to the small sample of giant planets orbiting low-mass stars and provides constraints on planet formation theories.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35703.title: pbhalo: computing primordial black hole and minihalo populations from a single primordial perturbation spectrum
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35703.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35703v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: An enhancement of the primordial curvature power spectrum on small scales can give rise to two populations of compact objects: primordial black holes (PBHs), which form during radiation domination, and dark matter minihalos, including ultracompact minihalos (UCMHs), which form from the same modes during matter domination. We present pbhalo, an open-source Python package that computes the PBH mass function, the halo mass function and the UCMH abundance from a single spectrum in a given cosmology and applies observational constraints on the PBH abundance and on the spectrum jointly. The package components are validated against colossus (a code for halo mass functions and cosmological quantities), pbhstat (a code for the PBH mass function from a given spectrum) and published results; joint constraints are illustrated for lognormal peaks. The code is distributed under the MIT license.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.39785.title: Robust statistical significance for Gravitational Wave inference
arxiv.org/abs/2610.39785.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.39785v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on Bayes factors to make astrophysical statements about detected signals. This is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of orbital precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. For the latter, a main limiting factor is the growing bias resulting from accumulating per-event uncertainties related to stochastic sampling. In both cases, the computational cost of calculating Bayes factors severely limits the astrophysical usefulness of the results: Though Bayes factors robustly quantify the data's preference towards one model, one cannot generally determine how likely an equally large value is to arise under the null hypothesis. This paper applies evidence networks, amortized neural estimators which can infer Bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between two datasets, to the aforementioned problems. This makes it possible to construct empirical Bayes factor distributions under different signal assumptions, providing a calibration between observation and discovery significance. Using simulated Gaussian noise, we apply this method to a search for orbital precession in gravitational-wave data and achieve compatible results to current state-of-the-art approaches that require stochastic sampling. We further show that high precision of the achieved results leads to recovering injected isotropic-spin population fractions without discernible bias for populations of up to $10^4$ events on a simplified example. More generally, because the method does not require explicit likelihood evaluations, this lays a clear path towards a likelihood-free framework that does not rely on the assumption of Gaussian and stationary noise.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.41355.title: Stellar Bars Reshape the Spatial Distribution of UV-bright Clumps in Nearby Galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2610.41355.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.41355v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Stellar bars redistribute gas and angular momentum in disk galaxies, but whether they mainly change the amount or the spatial organization of recent star formation remains uncertain. We use archival HST/WFC3 F275W imaging to study 70 barred galaxies and 95 unbarred control galaxies matched in stellar mass, optical color, redshift, and F275W background noise. A uniform dendrogram-based procedure identifies 95,486 UV-bright star-forming clumps. We compare their radial and azimuthal distributions, central F275W emission, and luminosity and size distribution functions. Relative to their controls, barred galaxies show a deficit of clumps at intermediate radii broadly corresponding to the bar region, followed by a local recovery near the bar ends. Their clumps are also preferentially concentrated along the bar major axis. These spatial differences are stronger in high-mass galaxies. Normalized bar length is more closely associated with the radial redistribution and central F275W concentration than bar ellipticity, although its relation to the azimuthal distribution is less uniform. When galactocentric radius is normalized by bar length, the recovery occurs near $R/R_{\rm bar}\sim1$, indicating that the bar sets a characteristic scale for the redistribution. Despite these spatial differences, barred and control galaxies have broadly similar clump luminosity and size distribution functions. Our results suggest that stellar bars mainly reorganize where recent star formation occurs, rather than substantially altering the observed luminosities and sizes of individual UV clumps, and that this effect depends on galaxy mass and bar extent.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.05086.title: von Neumann Stability Analysis of Braginskii MHD: Thermal Conduction, Viscosity, Magnetic Diffusion, and Thermoelectric Effects; and an Implementation in Athena++
arxiv.org/abs/2611.05086.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.05086v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Athena++ is a finite-volume astrophysical magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code. As of writing, isotropic thermal conduction and kinematic viscosity, Ohmic resistivity, and ambipolar diffusion are present in the main branch. Here we present a fork of Athena++, ``Athena-Aniso''. It implements fully anisotropic thermal conduction (parallel, perpendicular, and the Righi--Leduc effect); anisotropic viscosity (all five Braginskii viscosity tensors); the Hall effect; and several thermoelectric effects (Peltier, Seebeck, Nernst, and Ettingshausen). These effects can be weighted by ionisation fraction in a partially ionised gas, with the neutral part diffusing isotropically. We have also added isotropic bulk viscosity. The Biermann battery is not implemented here. The dissipative terms have super-time-stepping support, while the non-dissipative terms are combined with the ideal MHD flux. A CFL condition for all terms is derived and implemented using von Neumann stability analysis. The dissipative terms are found to be stable under first-order time integration. The non-dissipative terms are found to be stable under third-order time integration. We additionally derive new signal speeds for a modified HLLE Riemann solver. These suppress grid-scale non-linear instabilities still present in the non-dissipative terms. The Nernst/Ettingshausen system is found to be ill-posed unless it is stabilised by both perpendicular thermal conduction and perpendicular magnetic diffusion. We derive a well-posedness criterion for this. We provide numerical tests of each implemented effect against derived analytical solutions.

arxiv.org/abs/1303.1523.title: Inflation, Cosmic Perturbations and Non-Gaussianities
arxiv.org/abs/1303.1523.excerpt:
arXiv:1303.1523v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We review the theory of inflationary perturbations. Perturbations at both linear and nonlinear orders are reviewed. We also review a variety of inflation models, emphasizing their signatures on cosmic perturbations.

arxiv.org/abs/2510.27188.title: Magnetically supramassive and hypermassive compact stars
arxiv.org/abs/2510.27188.excerpt:
arXiv:2510.27188v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: It is known that the mass of a magnetized relativistic compact star is larger than that of non-magnetized one for the same equation of state and central density, albeit the excess of mass is sizable only if the magnetic fields are strong enough, B~10^17-10^18G. Using our recently developed numerical code COCAL, we systematically compute such compact star solutions in equilibrium associated with mixed poloidal and toroidal magnetic fields, and show the magnetically supramassive solutions whose masses exceed by more than 10% the maximum mass of the static and spherically symmetric solutions. For some extremely strong magnetic field configurations, we also obtain solutions more massive than the maximum mass of the uniformly rotating solutions at the Kepler (mass-shedding) limit, namely magnetically hypermassive solutions.

arxiv.org/abs/2511.19898.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
arxiv.org/abs/2511.19898.excerpt:
arXiv:2511.19898v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.

arxiv.org/abs/2512.17695.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
arxiv.org/abs/2512.17695.excerpt:
arXiv:2512.17695v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.18416.title: Classical and quantum evolution of inflationary fluctuations
arxiv.org/abs/2604.18416.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.18416v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We compare the correlation functions of inflationary perturbations computed either with quantum or classical dynamics. Even if they are enforced to agree at a specific time during inflation, classical and quantum correlations will differ at the end of inflation, provided that interactions are relevant. The difference between the results of the classical and quantum computations is exponentially sensi- tive to the number of e-folds elapsed from the time of agreement. We illustrate this finding with the tree-level bispectrum of the primordial curvature fluctuation and the one-loop power spectrum of tensor modes. We also show that classical evolution from a finite time does not imply the appearance of poles in the scalar bispectrum.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.19880.title: Ultra-High-Energy Tau Neutrinos as Probes of Lorentz Invariance
arxiv.org/abs/2604.19880.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.19880v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neutrino telescopes have detected astrophysical neutrinos with energies up to ${O}(100)$ PeV. Several current and proposed experiments aim to observe neutrinos at even higher energies, with the goal of detecting cosmogenic neutrinos. This increase in neutrino energy makes tests of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) particularly appealing, since the effects of higher-dimension LIV operators on neutrino propagation grow rapidly with energy. In this work, we investigate the potential of the upcoming experiments GRAND and POEMMA to probe LIV in the neutrino sector through the detection of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos. We generate the cosmogenic neutrino flux using SimProp and interface it with a calculation of neutrino flavor transition probabilities in the presence of LIV effects. Deviations from standard flavor transition probabilities manifest as changes in the expected tau neutrino event rates at GRAND and POEMMA. We first consider the case with a single nonzero LIV operator of various dimensions, and find that the projected sensitivities exceed existing limits from lower-energy probes by orders of magnitude. We then explore scenarios with multiple nonzero LIV parameters and show that their interplay can significantly modify the sensitivities compared to the single-parameter case. Overall, we find that upcoming observations of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos will place some of the most stringent constraints on LIV.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.21658.title: Towards LLM-Powered Automation of a Dark Matter Constraint Repository
arxiv.org/abs/2606.21658.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.21658v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Dark matter constraint repositories are critical community infrastructure, yet the most widely-used are volunteer-maintained, a sustainability risk as results accelerate. Limits are typically published as figures rather than machine-readable records, compounding the burden. We present a large language model (LLM) system that monitors arXiv, extracts limit curves, integrates them as code, and opens pull requests for human review. Extraction uses a tool-using agent that interprets physical conventions and checks its results, with a fixed multi-channel pipeline evaluated as an alternative. We evaluate both approaches on a 329-paper benchmark of measured limits graded against the upstream-curated repository. An extraction is considered successful when the extracted and reference mass ranges overlap by more than 90%, with at least 90% of compared values agreeing within a factor of two. For Fable 5, 52.6% of eligible curve comparisons meet this criterion with the agent, compared with 20.9% with the pipeline. Deployed, the pipeline has generated limit proposals, but none have merged: governance of AI-generated scientific data is itself unsolved.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.09282.title: Leptogenesis with sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
arxiv.org/abs/2607.09282.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.09282v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.12497.title: Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis
arxiv.org/abs/2608.12497.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.12497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We propose a low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis scenario within the dynamical minimal scotogenic model for accommodating neutrino masses and inert scalar dark matter simultaneously. Thus, we dub the mechanism Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis. In this setup, a rolling Majoron arising from the global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry breaking induces an effective chemical potential for the $B-L$ charge in the presence of $B-L$ violating interactions that allow for the efficient decays and inverse decays of right handed neutrinos (RHN) and RHN mediated scattering, so it gives rise to the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe through the electroweak sphaleron conversion. The mechanism becomes effective in the strong washout regime and successfully lowers the viable mass scale of the lightest RHN to the range of TeV scales, thereby making the thermal scotogenic leptogenesis with two hierarchical RHNs accessible to direct tests. We identify the roles of the $\lambda_5$ coupling for spontaneous leptogenesis and inert scalar dark matter through the efficient erasure of the inert scalar asymmetry. We also explore the regime for Majoron dark matter from the kinetic misalignment, showing that a multicomponent dark sector comprising the inert scalar and the Majoron can be realized in the model. The resulting framework provides a unified origin for low-scale baryogenesis, neutrino masses, and multicomponent dark sector, so it can be tested by complementary experimental probes through direct detection experiments, collider searches for inert scalars, and future detection of Majoron dark matter or dark radiation.

universetoday.com/articles/earths-gravit.title: Earth's Gravity May Have Kept the Early Moon's Volcanic Heart Beating
universetoday.com/articles/earths-gravit.excerpt: We typically think of the Moon as a static, floating object that has remained the same for basically its entire lifetime, with an occasional asteroid impact serving as an exception. That understanding is grounded in physics - the Moon should have cooled rapidly after forming when a huge protoplanet hit the early Earth around 4.5 billion years ago. But, some lunar material returned from the Chang’e-5 mission was notably formed only around two billion years ago, yet appeared to be volcanic in origin. So how did a world that was supposed to have settled down without volcanism remain hot enough to create these materials more than two billion years after its violent birth? A new paper from Miao Chen of the Chengdu University of Technology and his colleagues, and recently published in the journal Planet, offers an explanation - tidal heating.

That's where enzyme engineering comes in—researchers make changes to an enzyme, test how those changes affect what the enzyme does and look for versions that work better.

7.summary: Simulations show that Lyman continuum escape fractions peak about 16 Myr after star‑formation bursts, especially in massive early galaxies.
highlights: Typical LyC escape lag is ~16 Myr with peak correlations of 0.4‑0.6 in massive haloes
Delay scales as M★⁻⁰·¹⁹ and Mhalo⁻⁰·²⁷, lengthening for lower‑mass systems
Hα‑to‑UV luminosity ratio retains a delayed link to LyC escape, offering an observable tracer

15.headline: Astrolabe Surrogate Generates Full‑Resolution Cosmology Simulations via Flow Matching
15.summary: Astrolabe uses a flow‑matching transformer to emulate particle‑level cosmology, delivering accurate large‑scale structure without voxel resolution limits.
highlights: Acts directly on 6N phase‑space coordinates of individual particles
Employs a hybrid transformer where each particle cross‑attends to multiscale field tokens
Matches physical flow using approximate COLA coordinates, preserving momentum and mass
Reproduces power spectra, halo mass functions, velocity and density profiles in Lambda‑CDM tests
Generalizes to dark‑acoustic oscillation initial conditions and scales to TNG50‑3‑dark size

3.headline: Vienna Researchers Unveil First Self-Stabilizing Thorium‑229 Nuclear Clock
3.summary: A team at TU Wien built a self‑stabilizing nuclear clock using thorium‑229 nuclei, achieving a precision of one‑second error over 30 million years.
highlights: The clock uses a laser‑driven transition in thorium‑229 nuclei to lock its frequency
It operates autonomously for over 24 hours without an external atomic reference
Measured relative precision reaches 10⁻¹⁵, far surpassing typical atomic clocks

8.headline: Rare FN1 Mutation Shields APOE ε4 Carriers from Alzheimer’s Brain Damage
8.summary: Scientists identified a protective FN1 mutation that limits fibrotic buildup around brain vessels, preserving blood‑brain barrier integrity in APOE ε4 carriers into their 80s.
highlights: APOE ε4 drives excess fibronectin accumulation around cerebral blood vessels
A rare FN1 mutation reduces fibronectin deposition and prevents barrier leakage
Single‑cell and spatial analyses confirmed the mechanism in mouse, zebrafish, and human tissue
Findings published in Nature Aging suggest new therapeutic targets for early Alzheimer’s intervention

11.headline: JWST Spectroscopy Reveals Common Mini‑Quenched Galaxies at z > 4
11.summary: Deep 28‑hour NIRSpec/PRISM observations in the OASIS program find that suppressed, mini‑quenched and lulling galaxies constitute a sizable fraction of early low‑mass galaxies.
highlights: Three mini‑quenched galaxies with log(M/Msun)=8.3‑8.9 lie 1.2‑1.7 dex below the star‑forming main sequence
Five lulling galaxies show weak Balmer emission just above the quenching threshold
Suppressed galaxies represent 29% of the sample at z=4‑5.5, with a number density ≈1.6×10⁻³ Mpc⁻³ dex⁻¹
Photometric estimates overstate star‑formation rates, misclassifying most candidates without spectroscopy

12.headline: Mineral‑Forming Techniques Capture Over 99% of Technetium‑99 from Waste
12.summary: Researchers at the University of Manchester have shown that engineered minerals can lock more than 99% of radioactive Technetium‑99 from liquid waste into stable forms.
highlights: Layered double hydroxides incorporated Technetium‑99 into their octahedral layers, achieving >99% removal from solution.
Methylene diphosphonic acid formed a soluble Tc‑MDP complex captured by hydroxyapatite, removing up to 99% in flowing
Advanced X‑ray analysis at Diamond Light Source confirmed mineral incorporation, and microbes were shown to aid Tc‑MDP complex

2610_09748v1.headline: Neutrino Current May Explain Cosmic Birefringence and Helium-4 Anomalies
2610_09748v1.summary: A new study links isotropic cosmic birefringence to a large lepton asymmetry via a Chern‑Simons coupling between the neutrino current and photons.
highlights: First analysis of anisotropic birefringence sourced by lepton-number isocurvature fluctuations on large scales.
On small scales, gravitational effects dominate over axion‑like particle (ALP) scenarios.
A large lepton asymmetry from the Affleck‑Dine mechanism can reproduce the observed isotropic birefringence.
The model may connect to low helium‑4 abundances reported by Subaru EMPRESS and ACT.

nanograv_15yr_fdmodel.headline: Legendre Models Sharpen Pulsar Timing, Cutting Profile‑Evolution Errors by Up to 85%
nanograv_15yr_fdmodel.summary: New Legendre‑based profile‑evolution formulas reduce timing‑delay residuals up to 85% and lower dispersion‑measure bias, improving nanohertz gravitational‑wave searches.
highlights: Legendre polynomial expansion (LIFD) predicts delays far closer to true profile evolution than traditional FD log‑polynomial
Residual timing offset improves by as much as 85% in simulated data when using LIFD.
FD‑based models overestimate injected DM by 0.013 pc cm⁻³, while LIFD reduces the error to 0.0002 pc cm⁻³.

arxiv_2610_08903v1.headline: Strongly‑Lensed Superluminous Supernova at z = 2.0155 Reveals Extreme Stellar Death and Galaxy Feedback
arxiv_2610_08903v1.summary: Astronomers used Keck‑II/KCWI spectroscopy and Pan‑STARRS photometry to study the highly magnified SLSN 2025wny, finding a magnetar engine and powerful outflows at cosmic noon.
highlights: Rest‑frame UV spectra obtained 11–61 days after peak with Keck‑II/KCWI
Magnification of the brightest image measured at μ_A = 19.4 ± 1.6, exceeding model predictions
Magnetar spin period P_spin = 4.1^{+0.7}_{-1.0} ms and field B_⊥ ≈ 2.4×10^{14} G fit the early light curve

arxiv_2610_08947v1.headline: SPT-3G Detects Record‑High Clustering of tSZ‑Selected Galaxy Clusters
arxiv_2610_08947v1.summary: A five‑year SPT‑3G survey measured galaxy‑cluster clustering at 12.8σ, yielding a halo bias of 5.30±0.24 and tightening mass‑observable constraints.
highlights: Cluster clustering detected at 12.8σ, the strongest tSZ‑selected signal to date
Halo bias measured as bₕ = 5.30±0.24 for clusters spanning 0.25 < z < 1.1
Normalization of the mass‑observable relation constrained to lnAₛz = 0.43⁺⁰·¹⁷₋₀·₂¹

arxiv_2610_08931v1.headline: Stellar Feedback Sparks Early Hot Corona Around Milky Way‑type Galaxies
arxiv_2610_08931v1.summary: Simulations show that stellar feedback can generate a hot circumgalactic medium as early as redshift 3, far earlier than accretion‑shock models predict.
highlights: Stellar feedback drives hot CGM formation at $z\approx3$, reaching virial temperatures.
Feedback‑free runs fail to produce comparable CGM temperatures before $z\lesssim1$.
Hot corona emergence triggers CGM virialisation within ≤0.5 Gyr, often outside‑in.
The apparent evolution of the corona is largely due to “pseudo‑evolution” of $R_{\mathrm{vir}}$.

arxiv_2610_08999v1.headline: Euclid Survey Reveals Shifting Quenching Mechanisms Across Cosmic Time
arxiv_2610_08999v1.summary: Analysis of Euclid Q1 data shows that recently quenched galaxies become less common over time, with fast quenching dominating massive early galaxies and slow quenching later.
highlights: Fast‑quenching efficiency peaks in massive galaxies at z>1.5
Slow‑quenching efficiency rises below z≈1.5, shifting toward intermediate masses
Most recently quenched galaxies at z<0.5 inhabit low‑density environments
fRQGs retain disc‑like morphologies while sRQGs become more concentrated

genetic_code_break.headline: Genetic Code Breakthrough: Protist Reassigns Two Stop Codons to Different Amino Acids
genetic_code_break.summary: A newly identified freshwater ciliate rewrites two universal stop signals, TAA and TAG, to encode lysine and glutamic acid, challenging long‑held genetic code rules.
highlights: The organism Oligohymenophorea sp. PL0344 uses TAA for lysine and TAG for glutamic acid
Only TGA remains a conventional stop codon in this protist
Discovery published in PLOS Genetics (Oct 2023) after testing a single‑cell DNA sequencing method
Follow‑up work (Dec 2024) found similar codon reassignments in five other ciliates
Researchers involved Dr Jamie McGowan (Earlham Institute) and Prof Thomas Richards (University of Oxford)

6.headline: ALMA Detects Water, Methanol and Methyl Formate in HD 100546 and IRS 48 Disks
6.summary: ALMA band 5 observations reveal methanol‑rich IRS 48 with no water, while HD 100546 shows both water and methanol, yielding a comet‑like CH₃OH/H₂O ratio.
highlights: IRS 48 disk shows methanol detection but water vapor remains undetected, giving methanol‑to‑water column ratio >0.2.
HD 100546 disk contains water and methanol with CH₃OH/H₂O ≈0.02, matching the median cometary value.
Methyl formate‑to‑methanol ratio is ~0.2 in IRS 48 and ~2 in HD 100546, indicating chemical enhancement in the latter.
Non‑LTE analysis constrains optical depths and emitting regions of methanol lines in both disks.

einstein_probe_neutron_star_phase.headline: Einstein Probe Uncovers Hidden Ten‑Minute Soft X‑Ray Phase in Neutron Star Mergers
einstein_probe_neutron_star_phase.summary: A wide‑field soft X‑ray monitor detected nearly ten minutes of emission after a short gamma‑ray burst, revealing a previously missed merger phase.
highlights: Soft X‑ray emission persisted for ~10 minutes after the initial sub‑second gamma‑ray flash
The prolonged signal likely originates from a newly formed magnetar central engine
Multi‑wavelength follow‑up confirmed the event as a compact‑object merger, not a supernova
Einstein Probe’s wide‑field capability captured a phase missed by Swift BAT and similar missions

fastest_star_black_hole_spin.headline: Fastest Milky Way Star S301 Circles Black Hole, Offering Spin Clues
fastest_star_black_hole_spin.summary: Astronomers have identified star S301 orbiting Sagittarius A in an 8.7‑year, ultra‑eccentric path, enabling a direct probe of the black hole’s spin.
highlights: S301 completes an 8.7‑year orbit with eccentricity ≈ 0.98, bringing it within 1.78 billion km of Sagittarius A
At pericentre the star reaches ~25,000 km s⁻¹, the highest speed measured for any Milky Way star
Its orbit shows ~2° Schwarzschild precession per revolution and a detectable Lense‑Thirring wobble

buffalo_survey_subhalo_mass_function.headline: BUFFALO Survey Maps Subhalo Mass Function in Merging Cluster Abell 2744
buffalo_survey_subhalo_mass_function.summary: A combined strong‑ and weak‑lensing analysis using HST and JWST data reveals an excess of substructures in the massive cluster Abell 2744 (z = 0.308).
highlights: Strong‑lensing constraints and deep weak‑lensing imaging from HST and JWST were merged to map mass from core to outskirts
The derived subhalo mass function shows more detected subhalos than predicted by BAHAMAS ΛCDM simulations
The excess likely reflects Abell 2744’s highly disturbed dynamical state rather than new physics

dark_siren_cosmology_catalog_completenes.headline: Fainter Galaxies Barely Shift Dark Siren Cosmology in GWTC‑3 Study
dark_siren_cosmology_catalog_completenes.summary: A new analysis of GWTC‑3 events shows that adding dimmer galaxies from the GLADE+ catalog generally does not alter dark‑siren cosmological estimates, except for GW190814.
highlights: Including galaxies fainter than the standard magnitude cut has negligible impact on joint cosmological constraints for most
The well‑localized binary merger GW190814 shows a measurable shift when fainter galaxies overlap its redshift range.
Redshift distributions reveal that most dimmer galaxies lie beyond the distances of the majority of dark sirens.
Future deeper catalogs could make faint‑galaxy contributions significant for multi‑event analyses.

el_nino_temp_record_2026.headline: Central Pacific Ocean Hits Record 86°F, Hinting at Super El Niño
el_nino_temp_record_2026.summary: Sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region surpassed 86 °F (30 °C) for the first time, signaling an unprecedented warming episode.
highlights: Record‑breaking 86 °F (30 °C) observed in the Niño 3.4 zone
Anomaly now 6 °F (3.34 °C) above average, far exceeding typical El Niño peaks
Experts label the event a potential “super” El Niño driven by climate change
Forecasts suggest temperatures could reach 7.2 °F (4 °C) above average by November
Research links this extreme event to shifting patterns of central‑Pacific El Niños

gravitational_lenses_desi_2026.headline: AI uncovers 70 new gravitational lenses in massive DESI sky map
gravitational_lenses_desi_2026.summary: Using AI on the 5.6‑trillion‑pixel DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, an international team confirmed 70 new gravitational lenses, expanding the premier lens catalog.
highlights: 70 gravitational lenses were spectroscopically confirmed with VLT‑MUSE
The search employed a residual neural network on data from DECam, MzLS and BASS
The new lenses join the DESI Strong Lens Foundry, one of the largest confirmed samples

electronic_stripes_vortex.headline: Charge Stripes Reveal Majorana Modes in Iron‑Based Superconductor Vortices
electronic_stripes_vortex.summary: Using atomic‑scale scanning tunneling microscopy, researchers observed charge‑stripe patterns intensifying around vortex cores, one of which hosts a Majorana zero mode.
highlights: Charge stripes strengthen near vortex centers in Ba(Fe₀.₉₄Co₀.₀₆)₂As₂ thin films.
Two distinct vortex states were identified, one containing a Majorana zero mode.
Spectroscopic‑imaging STM revealed the spatial correlation between stripes and vortex bound states.

milky_way_simulation_2026_10_08.headline: Milky Way once a swarm of thousands of galaxies, new simulations show
milky_way_simulation_2026_10_08.summary: New supercomputer simulations reveal that in the first two billion years after the Big Bang, the Milky Way region hosted thousands of tiny galaxies that later merged into today’s single spiral.
highlights: The Megatron suite tracks gas, starlight and chemistry from 180 million to 2 billion years after the Big Bang
JWST observations of bright early galaxies and “Little Red Dots” challenge previous models
The simulation predicts distinct spectral signatures that can be directly compared with JWST data

mantle_flow_pacific_2026.headline: Fossilized Mantle Flow Traced Beneath Pacific’s Oldest Oceanic Plate
mantle_flow_pacific_2026.summary: Ocean-bottom seismometers reveal complex, ancient mantle flow patterns beneath the 160‑180 million‑year‑old Pacific Triangle, challenging simple plate‑motion models.
highlights: Seismic anisotropy shows spatially variable orientations not explained by present‑day plate motion alone
Oldest-1 ocean‑bottom seismometer array (2018‑2019) captured shear‑wave data across the Pacific Triangle
Mantle flow appears redirected around a sunken remnant of lithosphere and near the Magellan Seamount Trail

high_res_global_atmospheric_model.headline: Tokyo Researchers Achieve 220‑Meter Global Climate Model, Erasing Popcorn‑Rain Bias
high_res_global_atmospheric_model.summary: A University of Tokyo team built a 220‑meter global large‑eddy simulation that removes the artificial ‘popcorn‑like’ rain bias, improving extreme‑weather forecasts.
highlights: Resolution narrowed to 220 meters, about the length of two soccer fields
Simulation used nearly 1 trillion grid points and over half of the Fugaku supercomputer
Eliminated the long‑standing popcorn‑like rain bias in global storm‑resolving models

interpretation_of_nanohertz_gravitationa.headline: Cosmic Strings May Explain Nanohertz Gravitational Waves, Study Finds
interpretation_of_nanohertz_gravitationa.summary: A Bayesian analysis of NANOGrav and EPTA data suggests a brief post‑BBN matter and kination era could produce the observed nanohertz gravitational‑wave background.
highlights: Bayes factor of 3.63 supports a transient matter‑kination phase
Cosmic‑string tension remains essentially unchanged
Analysis uses NANOGrav 15‑year and EPTA DR2 New+ datasets
Result holds even if supermassive black‑hole binary contribution is small

2610_11435v1.headline: Δ Baryons Enable Faster Neutron Star Cooling via Direct Urca Processes
2610_11435v1.summary: Incorporating Δ direct Urca neutrino emission into simulations shows that these channels can markedly accelerate the thermal evolution of neutron stars.
highlights: Δ direct Urca processes provide an efficient neutrino‑cooling mechanism
Simulations reveal significantly lower surface temperatures for Δ‑admixed neutron stars
First systematic study of Δ baryon weak‑interaction channels in neutron star cooling

2610_11881v1.headline: LHAASO Detects Orbital Modulation of PeV Gamma Rays from Cygnus X‑3
2610_11881v1.summary: New LHAASO observations show ultrahigh‑energy gamma‑ray emission from Cygnus X‑3 that varies with the binary’s orbit, revealing wind‑regulated particle acceleration.
highlights: GeV emission arises from anisotropic inverse‑Compton scattering of stellar photons by relativistic electrons
Multi‑PeV protons escaping the inner jet produce TeV‑PeV gamma rays via photohadronic and hadronuclear interactions
A fast accretion‑driven disk wind currently shields escaping protons from the dense Wolf‑Rayet wind, suppressing PeV output

2610_11045v1.headline: Galaxy Clustering Offers New Way to Pinpoint Binary Black Hole Host Types
2610_11045v1.summary: A novel method uses galaxy clustering within gravitational‑wave localization zones to statistically infer whether binary black hole mergers occur in star‑forming or quenched galaxies.
highlights: Event‑level host likelihoods are built from neighboring galaxy counts around each merger detection
Forecasts for O5, post‑O5 and third‑generation detectors predict 90% lower credible limits of 0.19, 0.48 and 0.92 for the
The approach works without assuming specific formation efficiencies or merger delay‑time distributions

primordial_black_holes_as_a_natural_cons.headline: Scale‑Invariant U(1) Theory Links Thermal Inflation to Primordial Black Holes
primordial_black_holes_as_a_natural_cons.summary: A scale‑invariant U(1) gauge model with a nonminimal Higgs‑gravity coupling naturally generates large curvature perturbations that seed primordial black holes and associated gravitational‑wave signals.
highlights: Nonminimal gravitational interaction ξ ≈ O(1) gives the Higgs a Hubble‑scale negative mass‑squared term
Thermal fluctuations at the end of thermal inflation amplify curvature perturbations enough to form PBHs across a wide mass range
Resulting PBH population predicts correlated scalar‑induced and cosmic‑string gravitational waves detectable by pulsar timing

2610_11588v1.headline: New Method Reveals Radial Flows in Disc Galaxies Using 3DBarolo
2610_11588v1.summary: A novel 3DBarolo workflow quantifies axisymmetric radial motions in disc galaxies, overcoming warp degeneracy and offering insights into gas accretion processes.
highlights: Developed a dedicated 3DBarolo workflow to measure axisymmetric radial velocities
Validated the method with realistic mock galaxies and TNG50 simulated Milky Way‑like discs
Bootstrapping provides robust uncertainty estimates for radial flow measurements
Analysis of TNG50 galaxies shows widespread local inflows/outflows but no global coherent radial flow

ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.institution: International collaboration (University of Glasgow, University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield, Kobe University)
ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.headline: Ultrafast XUV Spectroscopy Captures Excitonic Precursors in 1T‑TiSe₂
ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.summary: Using ultrafast broadband extreme‑ultraviolet absorption, researchers observed lingering excitonic correlations and heightened susceptibility near the 200 K transition in 1T‑TiSe₂.
highlights: UBXAS probed Se 4p and Ti 3d states with element‑specific resolution.
Excitonic response time scaled inversely with √laser fluence below 200 K.
Same fluence dependence persisted above the transition, indicating surviving excitonic interactions.
Near 200 K the response became ultra‑fast and fluence‑independent, revealing enhanced excitonic susceptibility.

molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.institution: University of Oxford and international collaborators
molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.headline: Oxford team captures molecular movie of penicillin biosynthesis
molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.summary: Using ultrafast XFEL snapshots, Oxford researchers revealed fleeting intermediates in penicillin’s β‑lactam ring formation, shedding light on antibiotic synthesis.
highlights: The enzyme isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS) was observed converting a linear peptide into the penicillin scaffold in real time
A thioaldehyde intermediate and a monocyclic β‑lactam intermediate were captured for the first time
Water molecules inside IPNS were shown to guide the reaction through precise proton transfers

2610_10741v1.headline: AI‑Driven 3D Gas Maps from Galaxy Surveys Enable Precise FRB Dispersion Measures
2610_10741v1.summary: A new generative model trained on the CAMELS50 simulation reconstructs three‑dimensional cosmic baryon density, improving FRB dispersion‑measure predictions across large volumes.
highlights: Model conditions on stellar‑mass weighted galaxy density, cosmological parameters, and baryon suppression power spectrum
Validated on test boxes, matching true DM per sightline and overall distribution
Scales to volumes ~4³ times larger than training, covering typical FRB cosmological paths
Provides a route to constrain feedback models using FRBs, X‑ray, SZ effect, and weak‑lensing

light_readout_mof_spin.institution: University of Glasgow (with partners University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield, Kobe University)
light_readout_mof_spin.headline: Light Reads Electron Spins in MOFs, Paving Way for Quantum Chemical Sensors
light_readout_mof_spin.summary: Researchers used optically detected magnetic resonance to read electron spin states inside a porous metal‑organic framework, opening a route to ultra‑sensitive quantum sensors.
highlights: First optical readout of spin resonance in a metal‑organic framework
Collaboration spans University of Glasgow, University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield and Kobe University
Technique could enable molecular‑scale detection of chemicals via a "quantum nose"

hidden_in_between_materials_for_batterie.headline: Hidden Intermediate Phases Reveal New β‑BiVO₄ Form for Solar Fuels and Batteries
hidden_in_between_materials_for_batterie.summary: Researchers at the University of Warwick uncovered transient material phases during heating, discovering a kinetic β‑BiVO₄ polymorph with a larger band gap and a lithium‑rich intermediate promising advances in solar‑fuel production and next‑generation
highlights: β‑BiVO₄ exhibits a distinct atomic arrangement and significantly larger band gap than known BiVO₄ forms
A lithium‑rich intermediate phase demonstrated high lithium storage capacity, hinting at battery applications
The study employed solid‑state NMR, X‑ray diffraction, and pair distribution function analysis to capture fleeting intermediates

bacteria_turn_a_virus_own_weapon_against.headline: Bacterial Immune System Uses Viral Enzyme to Trigger Self-Destruct Response
bacteria_turn_a_virus_own_weapon_against.summary: Scientists discovered that phage‑produced proteases cleave a bacterial CBASS sensor, activating a lethal suicide pathway that halts viral spread.
highlights: The viral protease cuts the bacterial sensor protein, acting as the alarm signal.
Activation of CBASS triggers an extreme “last‑resort” suicide response in the infected bacterium.
CBASS shares ancestry with a human immune pathway, indicating billions‑year evolutionary conservation.
Findings published in Science (2026) may improve phage‑therapy design against antibiotic‑resistant infections.

variable_water_clouds_jwst.headline: James Webb Telescope Captures Variable Water Clouds on Nearby Brown Dwarf
variable_water_clouds_jwst.summary: Using JWST, astronomers recorded the first real‑time changes in water‑cloud thickness on the cold brown dwarf WISE 0855, 7.5 light‑years away.
highlights: Water clouds on WISE 0855 thicken and thin as the object rotates
Carbon monoxide and phosphine signals reveal deep convective mixing
JWST’s medium‑resolution spectrograph delivered the most detailed time‑series portrait of a sub‑stellar atmosphere

frb_jwst_origin.headline: Young Galaxy Magnetar Powers Most Distant Fast Radio Burst Yet Seen
frb_jwst_origin.summary: A faint galaxy observed by JWST at 3 billion years old hosts FRB 20240304B, supporting a magnetar origin over neutron‑star mergers.
highlights: MeerKAT radio array precisely localized FRB 20240304B
JWST identified a small host galaxy at a cosmic age of ~3 billion years
Spectroscopy shows the galaxy’s stars formed within ~30 million years
The young stellar environment favors a magnetar over a neutron‑star merger origin
Findings are reported in arXiv preprint arXiv:2508.01648 (2025)

tiny_marine_microbe.headline: Tiny marine archaeon Candidatus Sukunaarchaeum mirabile boasts the smallest known genome yet retains full
tiny_marine_microbe.summary: Researchers uncovered the ultra‑reduced archaeon Candidatus Sukunaarchaeum mirabile, with just 189 protein‑coding genes, that still copies its DNA and makes proteins despite lacking nutrient‑production genes.
highlights: Genome size is less than half that of the smallest previously known archaeal genome
Contains only 189 protein‑coding genes yet retains DNA‑replication and protein‑synthesis pathways
Lacks genes for nutrient and energy production, suggesting reliance on a host or partner

quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.institution: University of California, Santa Barbara (or similar)
quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.headline: Quantum Chip Stores Multiple Photons for Over 1 Microsecond, Paving Way for Scalable Memory
quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana‑Champaign demonstrated a thin‑film lithium niobate chip that holds several photons simultaneously for more than a microsecond, a key step toward practical quantum memory.
highlights: Integrated nanophotonic platform uses erbium‑doped thin‑film lithium niobate
Atomic frequency comb technique enables multi‑photon storage exceeding 1 μs
Device shows high‑fidelity quantum information preservation and potential wafer‑scale manufacturing

fish_genes_urban.headline: Urban Coastal Waters Feed Fish but Trigger Hidden Genetic Stress
fish_genes_urban.summary: Blue damselfish thriving near Okinawa’s urban coastlines show abundant nutrition yet exhibit genome-wide stress signatures indicating chronic physiological strain.
highlights: Researchers sampled blue damselfish from 18 sites spanning pristine to heavily urbanized reefs in Okinawa
Genome-wide analysis identified 425 juvenile and 585 adult liver genes linked to urbanization
Urban fish displayed gene patterns similar to well‑fed lab fish but with heightened inflammatory responses
The study proposes a “junk food effect” where abundant food comes at a physiological cost

fast_two_photon_imaging.headline: Cornell Team Unveils Faster Two‑Photon Fluorescence Polarization Microscopy for Real‑Time Metabolism
fast_two_photon_imaging.summary: Researchers at Cornell have created a rapid two‑photon fluorescence polarization method that tracks NAD(P)H metabolism in live cells with minimal light exposure.
highlights: New two‑photon fluorescence polarization ratiometric microscopy (FPRM) reduces imaging time and light dose compared to
Polarization readout distinguishes protein‑bound versus free NAD(P)H, revealing cellular energy states instantly.
The technique works in three‑dimensional organoids, enabling dynamic metabolic studies in tissue‑like environments.

lunar_cave_mission.headline: NASA’s GIMLI Mission to Probe Lunar Pit for Hidden Lava Tube
lunar_cave_mission.summary: The GIMLI probe will map the Marius Hills Pit in Oceanus Procellarum, seeking the first on‑site evidence of a subsurface lunar lava tube.
highlights: GIMLI will deploy ground‑penetrating radar, a gravimeter, and seismic sensors to detect voids beneath the pit.
Mission led by the Planetary Science Institute with PI Than Putzig and built by Honeybee Robotics (Blue Origin).
A confirmed lava tube could shield future astronauts from radiation, micrometeoroids, and extreme temperature swings.
The project is funded through NASA’s PRISM program and will launch via the Commercial Lunar Payload Services partnership.

stratospheric_balloon_telescope_sunrise3.headline: SUNRISE III Balloon Telescope Uncovers Hidden Magnetic Threads in the Quiet Sun
stratospheric_balloon_telescope_sunrise3.summary: A 1 m solar telescope lifted to 35 km by a helium balloon revealed narrow 725 km magnetic threads with 10‑20 Gauss fields and opposite‑polarity intrusions in the quiet‑Sun chromosphere.
highlights: SUNRISE III used the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter (SCIP) to map full‑Stokes polarimetry of the solar
The observed magnetic threads are 725 km wide, with field strengths fluctuating between 10 and 20 Gauss, and show
MURaM‑ChE simulations reproduced these intrusions as twisted flux ropes 2,000‑7,000 km long
Magnetic field strength rises to ~40 Gauss above the solar limb, suggesting measurement differences due to spicule density

plastic_chemical_ovary.headline: Common Plastic Chemical DEHP Disrupts Multiple Human Ovarian Cell Types
plastic_chemical_ovary.summary: New eBioMedicine study shows that DEHP metabolite MEHP alters gene expression across diverse ovarian cells, including sensitive glial cells, at realistic exposure levels.
highlights: MEHP exposure changed expression of thousands of genes in seven ovarian cell types
Glial cells in the ovary were unusually sensitive to even low‑dose MEHP
Dose‑dependent effects were observed at 20.51 nM, an epidemiologically relevant concentration

type5_diabetes.headline: IDF Officially Recognizes Type 5 Diabetes, a Malnutrition‑Related Form
type5_diabetes.summary: The International Diabetes Federation’s 2025 decision names a fifth diabetes type linked to chronic nutrient deficiency, affecting up to 25 million people worldwide.
highlights: Type 5 diabetes, formerly MRDM, is estimated to affect up to 25 million people, mainly in low‑ and middle‑income regions.
The IDF created a working group in 2025 chaired by Meredith Hawkins to draft diagnostic criteria and treatment guidelines.
Studies show patients have insulin deficiency but retain insulin sensitivity, distinguishing them from Types 1 and 2 diabetes.
Existing insulin therapies can cause dangerous hypoglycemia in malnourished patients, prompting calls for tailored treatment.

4.headline: Chandra Reveals Kiloparsec-Scale Jet at Record-Breaking z=6.1
4.summary: Deep 360 ks Chandra observations resolve the distant AGN jet into two X‑ray components, showing a steep photon index and an 18% extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio.
highlights: Extended X‑ray emission splits into two slightly resolved components
Photon index of the jet is Γ = 2.25, steeper than the core’s Γ = 1.86
Extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio reaches 18%
Simulations suggest an AXIS‑like mission could boost photon counts by ~17×

1.headline: Hidden POLO Pathway Discovered: Eye’s New Lymphatic Drainage System
1.summary: Scientists at UBC and the University of Toronto identified a posterior ocular lymphatic outflow (POLO) in mice that clears fluid and waste from the retina, reshaping blindness research.
highlights: POLO pathway routes fluid from the choroid to orbital lymph nodes
Discovery challenges a century‑old view that the eye lacks lymphatics
Potential target for glaucoma and macular degeneration therapies
Study published in Translational Vision Science & Technology

cannabis_anxiety_brain_cells.headline: Cannabis Triggers Anxiety via Activation of Central Amygdala Somatostatin Neurons
cannabis_anxiety_brain_cells.summary: A Nature Communications study shows that high‑dose cannabinoids boost activity of CeA somatostatin neurons in mice, intensifying anxiety‑like defensive behaviors.
highlights: Mice given the synthetic cannabinoid CP 55,940 froze longer when exposed to a predator odor
Activation of CeA SOM neurons increased dose‑dependently with cannabinoid exposure
Blocking SOM neuron output reduced the anxiety‑like response despite cannabinoid administration
The effect was observed using implanted miniature microscopes to record neuronal activity

2610_12595v1.headline: Hubble Constant Measured to 3% Precision Using Lensed Supernova SN Refsdal
2610_12595v1.summary: A new analysis of the strongly lensed SN Refsdal in cluster MACS J1149.5+2223 yields H₀ = 65.0⁺²·⁰_₋₁·⁸ km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ with 3% uncertainty.
highlights: H₀ measured at 65.0⁺²·⁰_₋₁·⁸ km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ (3% precision)
Incorporated 77,000 HST pixels, halving the H₀ uncertainty compared to previous lens models
Simultaneous estimate of matter density Ω_m = 0.30⁺⁰·⁰⁸_₋₀·⁰⁹ within flat ΛCDM

2610_12947v1.headline: Future Gravitational‑Wave Detectors Could Uncover Helicity in Primordial Waves
2610_12947v1.summary: A new study proposes a universal helicity efficiency coefficient to gauge how upcoming GW observatories might detect parity‑violating signals across a vast frequency range.
highlights: Introduces a helicity efficiency coefficient that unifies sensitivity estimates for diverse GW detector designs
Shows that both regular and irregular tensor solutions can carry opposite helicities, complicating net‑helicity interpretation
Applies the metric to forecast detection prospects for future experiments spanning twenty orders of magnitude in frequency

jwst_cosmos_emissionlinesurvey.headline: JWST Slitless Survey Maps 12,000 Emission‑Line Galaxies Across Cosmic History
jwst_cosmos_emissionlinesurvey.summary: Using JWST/NIRCam WFSS, the COSMOS‑3D team cataloged 12,275 galaxies from redshift 0 to 9, revealing star‑formation and AGN signatures with unprecedented depth.
highlights: 0.33 deg² area covered with F444W grism spectroscopy
3σ line‑flux limit of 3.2×10⁻¹⁸ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²
AI‑driven pipeline combines CNN and large‑language model for source identification
